lessons.title: Risk management & contingency planning
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre riscos de uma obra e planos de contingência usando frases simples em inglês com clientes norte-americanos.
lessons.overview:
Risk management is one of the most strategic topics in the daily life of a senior construction executive. At Racional, every large project, such as a data center for Microsoft or Amazon, brings risks of schedule, cost and safety. Knowing how to talk about risk management in English shows the client that the company has control and maturity.

A North American client values directness. They want to hear, clearly, what the worst-case scenario is and what the contingency plan is. In projects of 18 to 24 months, supplier delays or scope changes are common, and the executive needs to explain how Racional will mitigate each risk before it turns into a problem.

In this lesson you will learn how to identify a risk, describe its impact, and present a safeguard. These are short, confident sentences for governance meetings, where the client expects to hear a leader who sees risk early and acts with calm and a defined plan.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três estruturas-âncora: "We see a risk in..." (Vemos um risco em...), "Our plan is to..." (Nosso plano é...) e "If that happens, we will..." (Se isso acontecer, nós vamos...).

Pratique também o verbo to mitigate (reduzir/mitigar) e a expressão contingency plan (plano de contingência).
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de governança, um cliente norte-americano pergunta a Cássio quais são os principais riscos da obra de um data center e como a Racional vai lidar com eles.
lessons.context: Every project has risks. On a big build, the main risks are time, cost and safety. Our team finds each risk early. We look at the impact and how likely it is. Then we make a plan. For each risk, we have a backup plan. If a supplier is late, we have a second supplier. We keep a safety buffer in the budget. We talk to the client about every risk. We want no surprises. A good plan keeps the project on track.

vocab.example: Risk management is part of every project.
We have a contingency plan for delays.
We identify a risk early.
This risk has a small impact.
The likelihood of a delay is low.
We mitigate the risk with a buffer.
Our cost exposure is low this month.
The worst-case scenario is a two-week delay.
We keep a safety buffer in the budget.
Our fallback is a second supplier.
We use early warning signs to act fast.
A supply delay can stop the work.
I flag a risk as soon as I see it.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos são a base para falar de risco em reuniões de governança.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a melhor resposta
exercises.prompt: O cliente pergunta sobre um atraso de fornecedor. Como você apresenta a proteção?

options.text: We have no plan for that.
options.whyWrong: Passa insegurança; o cliente quer ouvir que existe um plano.

options.text: We have a fallback. We use a second supplier.
It is not our problem.
options.whyWrong: Soa pouco profissional e quebra a confiança do cliente.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: We ___ the risk with a safety buffer in the budget.
exercises.explanation: "To mitigate" significa reduzir o risco. "Reduce" também é aceito.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva uma resposta curta
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases explicando um risco da obra e o plano para reduzi-lo. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula.
exercises.modelAnswer: We see a risk in the supply of steel. Our contingency plan is to use a second supplier.
exercises.explanation: A correção observa apenas o uso correto dos termos de risco.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: We see a risk here, but we have a contingency plan.
exercises.translation: Vemos um risco aqui, mas temos um plano de contingência.
exercises.prompt: Diga esta frase com calma e segurança, como em uma reunião de governança.
exercises.explanation: Tom firme e tranquilo transmite controle ao cliente norte-americano.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por cerca de 15 segundos, descreva um risco da obra de um data center e diga qual é o seu plano de contingência para reduzi-lo.
takeaways: I can name the main risks of a project.
I can explain a contingency plan in simple words.
I can say how we mitigate a risk.
I can talk about the worst-case scenario with a client.

flow.how: Em pé, repetição coral das frases-chave; acelere o ritmo a cada rodada.
Construa a frase de trás para frente, repetindo em blocos até a frase inteira.
Encene o cenário; depois troquem de papel.
Aplique o alvo a uma situação real do projeto do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.

practiceBank.title: Reunião de governança: top 3 riscos da obra
practiceBank.how: Professor é o cliente norte-americano e pergunta 'What are the main risks of this project?'. Cássio responde apresentando 3 riscos, cada um com impact e likelihood, e como vai mitigate cada um. Professor cobra detalhes ('What's the worst-case scenario?') para forçar uso do vocab. Foco em frases completas e claras.
lines: Set it: 'I'm your US client. What are the main risks of this data center project?'
For each risk probe: 'What's the impact, and what's the likelihood?'
Push: 'And how will you mitigate that one?'
Pressure: 'What's the worst-case scenario here?'
Require: risk management, to identify a risk, impact, likelihood, to mitigate. (Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Matriz de risco incompleta
practiceBank.how: Cada lado recebe metade de uma matriz de risco do data center (um tem impact, o outro tem likelihood). Sem mostrar o papel, eles perguntam e respondem para completar a matriz oralmente usando 'high/low impact' e 'high/low likelihood'. Professor monitora e anota erros para feedback no fim.
lines: Say: 'We each hold half the risk matrix. You have impact, I have likelihood. Don't show your sheet.'
Prompt him to ask: 'What's the likelihood of the chiller supply delay?'
Answer one cell at a time so he keeps asking.
Require the phrases: high/low impact, high/low likelihood.
Note: anote os erros para feedback no fim.

practiceBank.title: Qual risco mitigar primeiro?
practiceBank.how: Dê 5 riscos reais da obra (supply delay, falta de mão de obra, mudança de escopo do cliente, clima, falha de fornecedor). Cássio ranqueia do mais ao menos crítico e justifica cada posição usando exposure, impact e likelihood. Professor desafia o ranking pedindo 'Why is this one above that one?'.
lines: Say: 'Five real risks: supply delay, labor shortage, client scope change, weather, supplier failure. Rank them.'
After each ask: 'Why is this one above that one?'
Require: exposure, impact, likelihood.
Challenge: 'I'd rank scope change higher — convince me.'
Close: 'So which do we mitigate first?'

practiceBank.title: Pitch do contingency plan
practiceBank.how: Cássio grava 60 segundos explicando o contingency plan para um supply delay de equipamento crítico do data center, citando fallback, safety buffer e early warning. Depois ouve a própria gravação com o professor e refaz uma vez melhorando fluência e uso do vocab.
lines: Say: 'Record 60 seconds: your contingency plan for a critical equipment supply delay.'
Start him with: 'If the chillers are delayed, our contingency plan is...'
Require: fallback, safety buffer, early warning.
Play it back together, then say: 'Record once more — smoother, same vocab.'
Ask: 'What's the earliest sign you'd see the problem coming?'

practiceBank.title: Chegou um early warning
practiceBank.how: Professor descreve um early warning: o fornecedor de chillers avisa atraso de 3 semanas. Cássio precisa, ao vivo, flag the risk, explicar o impact na obra e propor a fallback. Professor reage como cliente preocupado e Cássio deve reassegurar com o plano.
lines: Set it: 'Early warning — your chiller supplier just announced a 3-week delay. React live.'
Prompt: 'Flag the risk for me and explain the impact on site.'
React as a worried client: 'Three weeks? That hits my go-live date.'
Push: 'What's your fallback? Reassure me.'
Require: early warning, to flag a risk, impact, fallback. (Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Rajada de perguntas sobre risco
practiceBank.how: Professor dispara perguntas rápidas alternadas ('What could delay the project?', 'How do you measure impact?', 'What's your safety buffer?'). Cássio responde em uma ou duas frases sem pausas longas, usando o vocab da aula. Velocidade aumenta a cada rodada.
lines: Say: 'Rapid fire. One or two sentences, no long pauses. Faster each round.'
Fire: 'What could delay the project?'
Fire: 'How do you measure impact?'
Fire: 'What's your safety buffer?'
Require: impact, likelihood, to mitigate, safety buffer, exposure.

practiceBank.title: Lendo a matriz impact x likelihood
practiceBank.how: Mostre uma matriz 2x2 (impact x likelihood) com vários riscos plotados. Cássio descreve onde cada risco está e o que isso significa para a obra ('This one is high impact, low likelihood, so we keep a fallback'). Professor pede para ele recomendar ações com base na posição.
lines: Show the 2x2: 'Impact versus likelihood, risks plotted. Describe where each one sits.'
Model: 'This one is high impact, low likelihood, so we keep a fallback.' → his turn.
Prompt: 'What does that position mean for the build?'
Push: 'Recommend an action for each quadrant.'
Require: impact, likelihood, exposure, to mitigate, fallback.

practiceBank.title: Vale a pena pagar pelo safety buffer?
practiceBank.how: Afirmação para debater: 'Manter um safety buffer grande é desperdício de dinheiro.' Cássio defende a posição contrária ao professor, argumentando com worst-case scenario e exposure. Professor banca o advogado do diabo cético sobre custo.
lines: Pose it: 'A big safety buffer is a waste of money. Argue the opposite to me.'
Play the skeptic: 'That buffer is just idle cash — cut it.'
Push: 'Show me the worst-case scenario that justifies it.'
Require: worst-case scenario, exposure, safety buffer.
Force balance: 'Now admit one case where I'd be right.'

practiceBank.title: A vez que um risco virou problema
practiceBank.how: Cássio conta uma história (real ou inventada) de uma obra em que um risco não foi mitigado a tempo. Deve usar to identify a risk, to flag a risk e contingency plan na narrativa. Professor ouve e no fim pergunta o que ele faria diferente.
lines: Say: 'Tell me about a project where a risk turned into a real problem.'
Require: to identify a risk, to flag a risk, contingency plan.
Prompt structure: 'Did anyone see it coming? What happened?'
Push: 'How did it hit the schedule?'
Close: 'What would you do differently next time?'

practiceBank.title: Frase obrigatória por carta
practiceBank.how: Embaralhe cartas com os termos da aula (mitigate, exposure, fallback, early warning, etc.). Cássio puxa uma carta por vez e cria na hora uma frase verdadeira sobre a obra do data center usando o termo. Professor só aceita se a frase fizer sentido técnico.
lines: Shuffle the cards: 'Draw one, make a true sentence about the data center build. Must be technically correct.'
Cards: mitigate, exposure, fallback, early warning, supply delay, to flag a risk.
If a sentence is vague: 'That's not technical — tie it to the actual site.'
Keep drawing until the deck is done.
Close: 'Which term is hardest for you to use? Do it once more.'

practiceBank.title: Conselho na cadeira quente
practiceBank.how: Cássio assume a cadeira quente como responsável pela obra. O professor e perguntas encadeadas pressionam: 'Convince me your contingency plan works.' Ele precisa sustentar a defesa por 2-3 minutos sem fugir do vocab de risco.
lines: Say: 'Hot seat. You own this build. Convince me your contingency plan works — for two minutes.'
Pressure: 'I don't believe your fallback is fast enough.'
Pressure: 'What if the early warning comes too late?'
Require sustained use: contingency plan, fallback, to mitigate, exposure, safety buffer.
Don't let him drift off the risk vocab. (Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Do PT para o pitch ao cliente
practiceBank.how: Professor diz frases curtas em português ('Identificamos o risco cedo e ativamos o plano de contingência'). Cássio traduz oralmente na hora para um inglês simples e correto. Foco em automatizar mitigate, to flag a risk e contingency plan.
lines: Say: 'I say a short Portuguese line, you translate to simple English immediately.'
'Identificamos o risco cedo e ativamos o plano de contingência.' → expect 'We identified the risk early and activated the contingency plan.'
'Esse fornecedor tem alto impacto e baixa probabilidade.' → expect 'This supplier is high impact and low likelihood.'
'Precisamos sinalizar esse risco para o cliente hoje.' → expect 'We need to flag this risk to the client today.'
Require automatic: to mitigate, to flag a risk, contingency plan.

leadIn: What are the top three risks on your data center project?
How do you measure the impact of a risk?
What's the difference between impact and likelihood for you?
What contingency plan do you have for a supply delay?
What is the worst-case scenario you plan for?

pill.tip: Em Nova Jersey e arredores, a vogal de "down" e "about" começa mais à frente e tensa, soando como "eh-oo" — "deh-oon" em vez de um 'a' aberto.
pill.sample: The numbers are down, so let's talk about next quarter.

lessons.title: M&A, joint ventures & strategic partnerships
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre parcerias, joint ventures e fusões com frases simples, mostrando o valor de unir forças com um cliente.
lessons.overview:
Growth through partnerships is a central topic on a senior executive's agenda. Racional, with more than 50 years and 620 projects, sometimes joins forces with other companies in a joint venture or in a strategic partnership to deliver large-scale projects, such as a shopping center or a hyperscale data center.

When the client is North American, they want to understand the logic of the deal: the strategic rationale and the synergy that each side brings. Talking about this in simple English helps the executive show that Racional knows how to choose partners, share risk, and create value in a clear and mature way.

In this lesson you will learn how to explain why a partnership makes sense, what each side brings to the table, and how the two companies grow together. These are direct sentences, useful for strategic conversations and for the start of the commercial cycle of a large project.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três estruturas-âncora: "We bring X to the table" (Trazemos X para a mesa), "Together we can..." (Juntos podemos...) e "We share the risk" (Dividimos o risco).

Lembre também das palavras joint venture (empreendimento conjunto) e synergy (sinergia).
lessons.situation: Cássio conversa com um cliente norte-americano sobre uma possível joint venture para construir e operar um grande shopping center juntos.
lessons.context: Sometimes two companies work better together. This is a partnership. In a joint venture, two firms build one project as a team. Each side brings something to the table. We bring local experience and a strong team. The partner brings money and market access. We share the risk and the cost. We also share the value. The goal is simple. Together we can do more than alone. A good partner makes the project stronger.

vocab.example: A merger joins two companies into one.
An acquisition is when one firm buys another.
We start a joint venture for the mall.
This is a strategic partnership for both sides.
The strategic rationale is clear and simple.
Together we create synergy.
We bring local experience to the table.
Both companies share the risk.
We do due diligence before the deal.
We combine strengths to grow faster.
The partner gives us market access.
Our skills are complementary.
Together we create value for clients.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: We bring local experience to the table.
exercises.explanation: "To bring to the table" significa o que cada lado oferece na parceria.

exercises.title: 2. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: Em uma joint venture, dividir risco e custo é a ideia central.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: We do ___ before we close the deal.
exercises.explanation: "Due diligence" é a auditoria prévia que confirma se o negócio é seguro.

exercises.title: 4. Escolha a melhor resposta
exercises.prompt: Como você explica por que a parceria faz sentido?

options.text: Our skills are complementary, so together we create value.
We do not need a partner at all.
options.whyWrong: Contradiz a ideia de parceria que está sendo proposta.

options.text: We want all the money for us.
options.whyWrong: Soa egoísta e quebra a confiança na joint venture.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Together we can do more than alone.
exercises.translation: Juntos podemos fazer mais do que sozinhos.
exercises.prompt: Diga esta frase com energia positiva, como ao fechar uma parceria.
exercises.explanation: É uma frase forte e simples para resumir o valor de uma parceria.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por cerca de 20 segundos, explique a um cliente por que uma joint venture entre a Racional e a empresa dele faz sentido: o que cada lado traz para a mesa.
takeaways: I can explain why a partnership makes sense.
I can say what each side brings to the table.
I can talk about a joint venture in simple words.
I can say that we share the risk and create value.

teacher.overview: M1 — Desenvolver vocabulário e fluência em inglês para que o executivo se posicione com naturalidade em conversações estratégicas — visão corporativa, governança, gestão de risco, condu…

flow.how: Professor e aluno de costas (ou câmera desligada): um descreve, o outro responde só pela voz.
Aluno passa a frase de afirmativa → pergunta → negativa, falando.
Professor faz 6-8 perguntas abertas; respostas faladas.
Grave 60s para o portfólio de fala do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição
flow.how: Feche SEMPRE por aqui: o aluno marca cada 'I can…' que já consegue dizer em voz alta. Ao marcar todos, a aula fica registrada como concluída e mais clara no programa. É assim que toda aula termina.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).

practiceBank.title: Propondo a joint venture do shopping
practiceBank.how: Cássio apresenta ao professor (cliente norte-americano) a ideia de uma joint venture para construir e operar um shopping center juntos. Deve explicar o strategic rationale, a synergy e o que cada lado bring to the table. Professor faz perguntas de quem ainda não está convencido.
lines: Set it: 'I'm a US client. Pitch me a joint venture to build and run a shopping mall together.'
Prompt: 'What's the strategic rationale here?'
Probe: 'Where's the synergy? What does each side bring to the table?'
Play unconvinced: 'I'm not sold — why not just hire you?'
Require: joint venture, strategic rationale, synergy, to bring to the table.

practiceBank.title: Quem traz o quê para a mesa
practiceBank.how: Em 6 minutos, Cássio e o professor negociam a divisão de responsabilidades da JV: quem entra com capital, terreno, operação. Cássio deve usar to bring to the table, to share the risk e complementary. Cronômetro à vista força decisão.
lines: Set it: 'Six minutes. We split the JV: capital, land, operations. Negotiate with me. Clock's running.'
Push: 'I'll bring the capital — what do you bring?'
Push: 'Who carries the construction risk?'
Require: to bring to the table, to share the risk, complementary.
Force a close: 'Time's nearly up — lock the split now.'

practiceBank.title: 30s para vender a sinergia
practiceBank.how: Cássio tem 30 segundos para convencer um investidor (professor) de que a parceria cria valor. Precisa encaixar synergy, to combine strengths e to create value. Faz duas vezes, encurtando e afiando na segunda.
lines: Say: 'Thirty seconds to convince me, an investor, that this partnership creates value. Go.'
Start him with: 'This partnership works because together we...'
Require: synergy, to combine strengths, to create value.
Run it twice: 'Sharper and shorter the second time.'
Ask: 'What's the single strongest line in that pitch?'

practiceBank.title: Dois perfis de empresa
practiceBank.how: Cássio conhece os pontos fortes da Racional; o professor conhece os do parceiro americano. Sem mostrar o papel, conversam para descobrir onde os pontos são complementary e montam juntos o caso da synergy. Professor anota usos do vocab.
lines: Say: 'You know Racional's strengths, I know the US partner's. Don't show your sheet — find the fit.'
Prompt him to ask: 'What does your side bring on technology?'
Answer so he must connect it to a Racional strength.
Require: complementary, synergy.
Close: 'Now state the synergy case out loud, together.'

practiceBank.title: Joint venture ou aquisição?
practiceBank.how: Tema: 'É melhor fazer uma joint venture do que uma acquisition.' Cássio defende a JV e o professor defende a acquisition. Cada um justifica com strategic rationale e to share the risk. Troca de lados no fim para praticar o vocab dos dois ângulos.
lines: Pose it: 'A joint venture is better than an acquisition. You defend the JV; I'll defend buying outright.'
Attack: 'An acquisition gives full control — JVs are messy.'
Push: 'Why share the risk instead of owning everything?'
Require: strategic rationale, to share the risk, joint venture, acquisition.
Swap sides at the end: 'Now argue for the acquisition.'

practiceBank.title: Cássio vira o investidor desconfiado
practiceBank.how: Inverta: Cássio é o cliente americano e o professor propõe a JV. Cássio faz a due diligence oralmente, perguntando sobre riscos, valor e sinergia. Isso o obriga a produzir perguntas com o vocab, não só respostas.
lines: Say: 'Now you're the skeptical US investor. I propose the JV. Run your due diligence on me.'
Prompt him to ask: 'What risks are you bringing into this?'
Prompt him to ask: 'Where exactly is the value and the synergy?'
Require in his questions: due diligence, to share the risk, strategic rationale.
Coach: 'Ask harder — investors don't take the first answer.'

lessons.title: Succession planning & talent management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre sucessão e desenvolvimento de talentos, mostrando ao cliente que a Racional tem um time forte e preparado.
lessons.overview:
A North American client who signs an 18 to 24 month contract wants to know whether the company will have prepared leaders throughout the entire project. That is why succession planning and talent management are strategic topics for a senior executive at Racional.

With 620 projects and 50 years of history, Racional has built a strong talent pipeline. Knowing how to explain, in simple English, how the company develops and retains its professionals reassures the client: the project does not depend on a single person.

In this lesson you will learn how to talk about the leadership team, how the company prepares successors, and how it keeps knowledge in-house. These are useful sentences for governance meetings and for building long-term trust with key accounts such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três estruturas-âncora: "We have a strong team" (Temos um time forte), "We develop our people" (Desenvolvemos nossa gente) e "We promote from within" (Promovemos de dentro).

Lembre das palavras successor (sucessor) e to retain (reter).
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião de governança, um cliente norte-americano pergunta a Cássio como a Racional garante liderança forte durante todo o projeto de 24 meses.
lessons.context: A long project needs strong leaders. We plan for this. We call it succession planning. We have a deep team, not just one person. We find key talent early. We develop our people every year. We mentor them. We promote from within. When a leader moves up, a successor is ready. This keeps the project safe. We also keep good people. We retain our best talent. A strong team is a strong promise to the client.

vocab.example: Succession planning keeps the team ready.
We have a strong talent pipeline.
We retain our best people.
Our retention is high this year.
We find key talent early.
We develop our people every year.
Senior leaders mentor young engineers.
A successor is ready for each role.
Continuity keeps the project safe.
We promote from within the company.
We support our high-potential people.
We onboard new leaders fast.
Knowledge transfer keeps the team strong.

lessons.title: Small talk & conversation starters
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá iniciar e manter uma conversa leve (small talk) com um cliente norte-americano antes de uma reunião.
lessons.overview:
Before every formal meeting there are a few minutes of light conversation, the small talk. For a senior executive at Racional, those minutes are worth gold: they are what create the human bond with a North American client over the 18 to 24 month cycle of a project.

The US business culture likes a quick and friendly small talk: asking about the trip, the weekend or the weather. Knowing how to break the ice with natural phrases makes the executive seem close and confident, even with simple English.

In this lighter lesson, the focus is genuine connection, not grammar. You will learn short and warm questions to welcome a client who has just arrived in São Paulo to visit a Racional project, such as a data center or a shopping center.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três aberturas naturais: "How was your trip?" (Como foi sua viagem?), "How's everything on your end?" (Como vão as coisas por aí?) e "Let's grab a coffee" (Vamos tomar um café).

Lembre da ideia de to break the ice (quebrar o gelo).
lessons.situation: Um cliente norte-americano acaba de chegar a São Paulo para visitar uma obra. Cássio o recebe com uma conversa leve antes da reunião.
lessons.context: It is good to start with small talk. Just a few friendly minutes. You can ask about the trip. "How was your trip?" You can ask about the weekend. People like easy questions. You break the ice. Then everyone feels relaxed. After a long flight, jet lag is normal. So keep it simple and warm. "Let's grab a coffee first." Small talk builds trust. Trust helps the long project.

vocab.example: Small talk helps people relax.
How was your trip to São Paulo?
When did you fly in?

vocab.pt: Como vão as coisas por aí?
vocab.example: How's everything on your end this week?
It's nice to catch up.
A simple question can break the ice.
Hi, how's it going?
Let's grab a coffee first.
Any weekend plans?
Did you settle in at the hotel?

vocab.pt: O que te traz a São Paulo?
vocab.example: So, what brings you to São Paulo?
Good to see you. It's been a while.
That was a long flight for you.
A little jet lag is normal.

lessons.title: Crisis communication & reputation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá comunicar uma má notícia ou um problema na obra de forma transparente, assumindo responsabilidade e reassegurando o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In long projects, problems happen: a delay, an unexpected technical issue, an incident. What defines a great executive is the way they communicate it. Crisis communication and reputation are strategic topics for Racional's leadership, which protects the brand built over 50 years.

The North American client values transparency and directness. They want to hear the executive take ownership, explain the root cause, and show the corrective action. Hiding the problem destroys trust; admitting it with a plan strengthens it.

In this lesson you will learn how to deliver difficult news with calm: acknowledge the problem, be direct, reassure the client, and promise to keep them informed. These are short, confident sentences for a delicate moment in a large project, such as a data center or hospital.
lessons.intro:
Vamos usar três estruturas-âncora: "Let me be straight with you" (Deixe-me ser direto), "We take ownership of this" (Assumimos a responsabilidade) e "We will get back on track" (Vamos voltar aos trilhos).

Lembre de to keep you posted (mantê-lo informado) e root cause (causa raiz).
lessons.situation: Há um atraso em uma obra da Racional. Cássio liga para o cliente norte-americano para comunicar o problema e o plano de correção.
lessons.context: Bad news is hard, but we share it fast. We are honest. "Let me be straight with you. We have a delay." First, we take ownership. The problem is ours to fix. Then we explain the root cause. After that, we share the corrective action. We tell the client the plan. "We will get back on track." We also reassure them. "We will keep you posted." Clear and honest words protect trust and our reputation.

vocab.example: Crisis communication must be clear and fast.
We protect our reputation with honesty.
We take ownership of the delay.
We acknowledge the problem.
We had a small setback this week.
Let me be straight with you.
We will get back on track soon.
I want to reassure you.
We act with full transparency.
We found the root cause of the delay.
Our corrective action starts today.
We will keep you posted every week.
Accountability builds trust.

Everything is perfect, no problems.

options.whyWrong: Fugir da responsabilidade enfraquece a reputação.

exercises.explanation: São os quatro passos de uma boa comunicação de crise.

exercises.explanation: A correção observa apenas o uso correto dos termos de comunicação de crise.

exercises.prompt: Diga com calma e firmeza, transmitindo controle da situação.
exercises.explanation: Diretividade calma é o que o cliente norte-americano espera em uma crise.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por cerca de 20 segundos, comunique a um cliente um atraso na obra: assuma a responsabilidade, cite a causa raiz e diga que vai mantê-lo informado.
takeaways: I can share bad news in an honest way.

practiceBank.title: A ligação do atraso
practiceBank.how: Sem vídeo, Cássio liga ao cliente para comunicar um atraso na obra. Deve abrir com to be straight with you, acknowledge o setback, take ownership e fechar com o plano de get back on track. Professor reage como cliente frustrado e Cássio precisa reassure.
lines: (Sem vídeo, atenda como cliente:) Hi Cassio, what's going on with the schedule?
(Reaja frustrado:) A delay? How long are we talking about?
(Pressione:) This affects our data center go-live. What's your plan?

(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Más notícias na reunião de obra
practiceBank.how: Cássio comunica presencialmente que houve um setback na obra do shopping. Deve manter a transparency, explicar a root cause e apresentar a corrective action. Professor pressiona sobre culpa e Cássio responde com accountability, sem se desculpar em excesso.

Espere root cause + corrective action, sem excesso de desculpas.

practiceBank.title: Concreto fora de especificação
practiceBank.how: Professor descreve a crise: um lote de concreto saiu fora da especificação e parou a obra. Cássio precisa, ao vivo, take ownership, explicar a root cause, a corrective action e como vai keep you posted. Professor reage exigindo prazo.
lines: Cenário: a batch of concrete came out off-spec and stopped the slab pour.
(Exija prazo:) When does work restart? Give me a date.
Espere ele: take ownership + root cause + corrective action + keep you posted.
(Adicione pressão:) And how do I know it won't happen again?
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: 60s de comunicação de crise
practiceBank.how: Cássio grava 60s comunicando uma má notícia com transparência: reconhece o problema, assume responsabilidade e reassegura. Deve usar to acknowledge, accountability e to reassure. Reescuta com o professor e regrava com tom mais firme e calmo.
lines: Start with: 'I want to be straight with you — we hit a setback this week.'
Em 60s: reconheça o problema + assuma responsabilidade + reassegure.
Required words: to acknowledge, accountability, to reassure.
Reescute e pergunte: did it sound calm and firm? Now record again, steadier.
Follow-up: where could you sound more confident?

practiceBank.title: Transparente vs. evasivo
practiceBank.how: Professor lê duas versões da mesma comunicação de problema: uma transparente e responsável, outra evasiva e defensiva. Cássio aponta oralmente as diferenças e refala a versão evasiva de forma transparente, usando to take ownership e transparency.
lines: Versão A (transparente): 'We made a mistake on the pour. I take full ownership. Here's our corrective action.'
Versão B (evasiva): 'Well, these things happen on site, it's not really anyone's fault.'
Pergunte: what makes version A more trustworthy?
Now say version B again, transparently, using to take ownership and transparency.

practiceBank.title: Cássio recebe a má notícia
practiceBank.how: Inverta: o professor (Racional) comunica um atraso e Cássio é o cliente americano. Cássio reage e faz as perguntas duras: 'What's the root cause?', 'How do you get back on track?'. Produz o vocab pelo ângulo de quem cobra.

Cassio, I'm calling because we've had a delay on the shopping center build.
(Espere ele fazer as perguntas duras:) What's the root cause? How do you get back on track?

practiceBank.how: Tema: 'Só se comunica um problema ao cliente quando já há solução.' Cássio defende a comunicação imediata e transparente; o professor defende esperar. Justificam com transparency, reputation e accountability. Trocam de lado no fim.
lines: Tema: 'You only tell the client about a problem once you already have a solution.'
Você defende comunicação imediata e transparente; eu defendo esperar.
(Contra-argumente:) But why worry the client before you can fix it?
Use: transparency, reputation, accountability. Depois troquem de lado.

practiceBank.title: Do e-mail furioso à ligação
practiceBank.how: Mostre um e-mail curto e irritado do cliente sobre o atraso. Cássio não responde por escrito: ele liga e responde oralmente, acknowledging o setback e dando a corrective action. Professor mede se ele acalmou o cliente.

Espere: acknowledge the setback + corrective action.
(Reaja como cliente:) Okay... that does make me feel a bit better. Go on.

practiceBank.title: Sob fogo cruzado do cliente
practiceBank.how: Cássio na cadeira quente: o professor faz perguntas duras e seguidas sobre o setback ('Who's responsible?', 'Why did this happen?', 'Will it happen again?'). Cássio sustenta a calma por 2-3 minutos usando accountability e to reassure sem fugir.

practiceBank.how: Em 6 minutos, após admitir o atraso, Cássio negocia com o cliente (professor) um novo prazo realista e medidas de compensação. Deve usar to get back on track e to reassure mantendo a transparency. Cronômetro força fechamento.

lessons.title: Corporate governance & compliance
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre governança e compliance, mostrando ao cliente que a Racional segue regras claras, auditorias e um código de conduta.
lessons.overview:
Governance and compliance are pillars of trust in any large contract. For North American clients such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google, corporate governance and compliance are not details: they are requirements. Racional, with 50 years and 620 projects, sustains its reputation precisely on clear rules.

A senior executive needs to explain, in simple English, how the company works: the board, the internal controls, the audits and the code of conduct. Showing that Racional is compliant and transparent reduces the risk perceived by the client and speeds up the decision.

In this lesson you will learn how to describe the governance structure and the commitment to rules and ethics. These are direct sentences, useful in meetings with the client's compliance and legal areas, common at the start of large projects such as data centers.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três estruturas-âncora: "We are fully compliant" (Estamos totalmente em conformidade), "We follow a code of conduct" (Seguimos um código de conduta) e "We are audited every year" (Somos auditados todo ano).

Lembre de board (conselho) e oversight (supervisão).
lessons.situation: A área de compliance do cliente norte-americano pede a Cássio uma explicação sobre a governança da Racional antes de assinar o contrato.
lessons.context: Big clients care about rules. They want a clear and honest company. We follow strong corporate governance. We have a board that gives oversight. We have internal controls for every project. We are compliant with the law and the regulations. We are audited every year. We follow a code of conduct. Everyone is accountable. We are transparent with the client. Clear rules and ethics build long-term trust.

vocab.example: We follow strong corporate governance.
Compliance is part of every project.
The board gives oversight.
We have internal controls for each step.
We are fully compliant with the law.
We follow every regulation.
An audit checks our numbers.
We are audited every year.
The board provides oversight.
Everyone here is accountable.
We follow a clear code of conduct.
The board must approve big decisions.
We are transparent with the client.
Ethics guide all our work.

takeaways: I can talk about corporate governance in simple words.
I can say that we are compliant and audited every year.
I can explain our code of conduct and internal controls.
I can say that we are transparent and accountable.

practiceBank.title: Explicando a governança ao compliance do cliente

practiceBank.how: Inverta: Cássio é o compliance do cliente e o professor representa a Racional. Cássio conduz a auditoria oralmente, fazendo perguntas com audit, oversight e code of conduct. Foco em formular perguntas de compliance.

lessons.title: ESG & sustainability na construção
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará, em inglês simples, sobre as práticas de sustentabilidade e ESG da Racional em uma conversa com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
For Racional's North American clients — such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google —, sustainability has stopped being a differentiator and has become a requirement. When a client decides to build a hyperscale data center or a large headquarters, they ask about carbon footprint, energy efficiency and green certification already in the first meeting.

As a board executive, you need to show that Racional has a clear ESG agenda: use of renewable energy, waste management and responsible sourcing of materials. Over more than 50 years and 620 projects, the company has also built its reputation by reducing the environmental impact of each project.

In this lesson you will learn how to say, in a short and direct way, that Racional is committed to net zero targets and that it takes care of the community impact. This vocabulary positions you as a serious partner in front of a demanding American client.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três frases-âncora: "We are committed to net zero by 2050.", "We use renewable energy on our sites." e "We reduce the environmental impact of every project."

Lembre-se: to be committed to sempre vem seguido de um substantivo ou de verbo com -ing.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião em São Paulo, um diretor da Microsoft pergunta como a Racional trata a sustentabilidade no projeto de um novo data center.
lessons.context: Sustainability is very important for us. We are committed to net zero. We use renewable energy on our sites. We manage waste and we recycle materials. Our goal is a low-carbon project. We also care about the local community. Safety comes first on every site. This is how we work.

lessons.title: Innovation & digital transformation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreverá, em inglês simples, como a Racional usa tecnologia e dados para dar mais previsibilidade às obras.
lessons.overview:
Racional's technology clients live on innovation and digital transformation. When Microsoft or Amazon hire a construction company, they want to know whether the project will be run with modern, data-driven methods, and not with loose spreadsheets and decisions made in the dark.

Racional uses BIM (building information modeling) to plan each project and dashboards to give the client real-time visibility. This helps to track progress and to streamline the workflow of large projects, such as hyperscale data centers.

In this lesson you will learn how to talk about this area in a short and clear way: how the company uses cutting-edge technology to offer delivery certainty from the moment it breaks ground. For the Racional executive, this vocabulary shows the American client that the company thinks like a technology company, and not only a concrete one.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: "We use BIM on every project.", "Our dashboard gives you real-time visibility." e "We track progress every day."

Repare que usamos o presente simples para falar de hábitos e processos da empresa.
lessons.situation: Um diretor da Amazon quer entender como a Racional vai dar visibilidade ao andamento da obra de um novo centro de distribuição.
lessons.context: Innovation is part of our work. We use BIM on every project. Our process is data-driven. We have a dashboard with real-time data. You can see the progress every day. This gives you full visibility. Technology helps us streamline the work and deliver on time.

vocab.example: Innovation is part of our work.
We invest in digital transformation.
Our process is data-driven.
We use BIM on every project.
Our dashboard shows the progress.

This gives you full visibility.
Technology helps us streamline the work.
We use cutting-edge tools.
We leverage data to plan better.
BIM improves our workflow.
We break ground in March.
We offer delivery certainty.
We track progress every day.

lessons.title: Regional differences (NE, South, Midwest, West Coast)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversará, em inglês simples, sobre as diferentes regiões dos Estados Unidos com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Racional's clients live in very different regions of the States (the United States). A client from the West Coast, in Seattle or California, tends to be more laid-back; whereas someone from New York, on the East Coast, tends to be more fast-paced and direct.

Knowing how to talk about the Midwest and the South creates connection. In the South, people are known for their hospitality and even use y'all (an informal way of saying "you all"). Asking about someone's hometown or about the local food scene is a great way to break the ice.

This is a relationship lesson. For the Racional executive, who works with North American clients on projects of 18 to 24 months, light conversation about regions helps the client feel at home. The goal here is not heavy grammar, but a genuine and human connection.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Where are you from in the States?", "People in the South are very friendly." e "I love the food scene there."

São frases simples para usar no início de uma conversa, antes da reunião de negócios.
lessons.situation: Antes de uma reunião, você conversa com um cliente do Google e descobre que ele é do Texas, no Sul dos EUA.
lessons.context: The United States is very big. The East Coast is fast-paced. The West Coast is more laid-back. People in the South are warm and friendly. The Midwest is calm and down-to-earth. Each place has a great food scene. I always ask people about their hometown. It makes them feel at home.

lessons.title: Change management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você explicará, em inglês simples, como a Racional conduz mudanças em um projeto e ganha o apoio do cliente.
lessons.overview:
In projects of 18 to 24 months, changes are normal: the client revises the scope, a new technology appears, or a deadline shifts. Change management is the way Racional handles these changes without losing control of the project and without losing the client's trust.

The secret is to get people's buy-in. When you explain the rationale for a change and use a phased approach, you reduce resistance and pushback. Keeping everyone in the loop helps to ease the transition.

For an American client, who values clarity and frankness, knowing how to communicate changes calmly is a sign of maturity. In this lesson you will learn how to say, in short sentences, that Racional will address concerns and ensure a smooth transition at every stage of the project.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We will roll out the change in phases.", "I want to explain the rationale." e "We will keep everyone in the loop."

Note o uso de will para falar de planos e do que a empresa vai fazer.
lessons.situation: O cliente da Microsoft pede uma mudança no escopo da obra e você explica como a Racional vai conduzir essa mudança.
lessons.context: Change is normal in a long project. We manage change with care. First, I explain the rationale. Then we roll out the change in phases. We keep everyone in the loop. This way we reduce resistance. Our goal is a smooth transition for the whole team.

vocab.example: Change management is part of our job.
We will shift to a new plan.
We roll out the change in phases.
We need buy-in from the team.
We want to reduce resistance.
We ease the transition step by step.

We use a phased approach.

vocab.en: to keep everyone in the loop

lessons.title: Stakeholder mapping & influence
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você falará, em inglês simples, sobre como identificar e engajar as pessoas-chave de um cliente.
lessons.overview:
In a large Racional project, there are many people involved. Knowing who the decision-maker is, who the influencer is, and who the gatekeeper is (the person who controls access) is essential. This work of mapping the stakeholders helps you know who to talk to and when.

Each person has a level of power and of interest in the project. The Racional executive needs to engage these people, align on objectives, and keep them informed. When you win over a champion (an internal advocate), it becomes easier to gain the buy-in of the whole client.

For American clients, who often have a decision committee and several approval levels, this mapping is decisive. In this lesson you will learn how to say, in short sentences, that Racional knows how to win over the right people and find a common ground with each of them.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We map all the stakeholders.", "Who is the decision-maker?" e "We want to find common ground."

Repare que 'stakeholder', 'decision-maker' e 'influencer' são substantivos para pessoas no projeto.
lessons.situation: Você planeja com sua equipe como engajar as pessoas-chave do cliente Google antes de iniciar um novo projeto.
lessons.context: Every project has many people. First we map the stakeholders. We find the decision-maker and the main influencer. We engage each person and we keep them informed. We look for common ground. This way we win their support.

vocab.example: We map every stakeholder.
Who is the decision-maker?
She is the main influencer.
First we map the stakeholders.
This person has a lot of power.
He has high interest in the project.
We engage each person.
We align on the main goals.
We keep them informed.
We need buy-in from the client.
She is our champion inside the company.
The assistant is the gatekeeper.
We want to win them over.
We look for common ground.

takeaways: I can talk about stakeholders in simple English.

practiceBank.title: Planejar engajamento dos stakeholders do Google

(Sugira um nome:) What about their facilities director? Friend or foe?

practiceBank.title: Explicar a matriz poder x interesse
practiceBank.how: O professor mostra uma matriz de stakeholders (power x interest). O aluno descreve onde cada pessoa fica e como tratá-la, usando 'power', 'interest', 'to keep informed' e 'champion'. O professor pede justificativa de cada posição.

practiceBank.title: Conquistar um gatekeeper

practiceBank.title: Mapa de stakeholders incompleto
practiceBank.how: Professor e aluno têm fichas parciais dos stakeholders do Google (um tem cargos, o outro tem nível de influência). Trocam perguntas para completar o mapa, usando 'decision-maker', 'influencer' e 'power'. Aluno produz perguntas e respostas.
lines: Information gap: você tem os cargos, eu tenho o nível de influência.
Troquem perguntas para completar o mapa de stakeholders do Google.

practiceBank.title: Quem engajar primeiro?
practiceBank.how: O professor lista cinco stakeholders do cliente e o aluno os ordena por prioridade de engajamento, justificando com 'decision-maker', 'champion' e 'to win over'. O professor questiona a ordem para gerar mais produção.
lines: Cinco stakeholders do cliente. Ordene por prioridade de engajamento e justifique.
(Questione:) Why engage the champion before the decision-maker?
(Provoque:) Is the gatekeeper really that low on your list?
Use: decision-maker, champion, to win over.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Identificação rápida de papéis
practiceBank.how: O professor descreve uma pessoa ('She controls the budget') e o aluno classifica rápido ('She's the decision-maker'), depois inverte. Treina 'influencer', 'gatekeeper', 'champion' em ritmo ágil.
lines: Rajada: eu descrevo a pessoa, você classifica rápido. Depois inverta.
'She controls the budget.' → (ex.: 'She's the decision-maker.')
'He blocks every meeting request.' → ?
'She loves our proposal and pushes it internally.' → ?
'He has no power but lots of opinions.' → ?
(Use: influencer, gatekeeper, champion.)

practiceBank.title: Mapear interesses do cliente
practiceBank.how: O aluno entrevista o professor (no papel de três stakeholders) sobre o que cada um quer do projeto, fazendo perguntas com o vocabulário da aula. Depois relata em voz alta ('The champion wants...'). Pratica perguntar e reportar.
lines: Faça-me perguntas (sou três stakeholders) sobre o que cada um quer do projeto.
(Como champion:) I just want this delivered on time, I'm rooting for you.
(Como gatekeeper:) I care about process — no surprises.
Depois reporte: 'The champion wants...', 'The gatekeeper wants...'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Um influenciador está contra o projeto
practiceBank.how: O professor diz que um 'influencer' importante está resistindo. O aluno propõe em voz alta como vai 'engage', achar 'common ground' e 'align on' objetivos. O professor adiciona obstáculos. Foco em solução falada.
lines: Cenário: an important influencer is resisting the project.
Proponha em voz alta como vai engage, achar common ground e align on objetivos.
(Adicione obstáculo:) Now he's telling others to doubt us too. What now?
Espere: to engage, common ground, to align on.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Pitch de 60s para um champion
practiceBank.how: O aluno faz um pitch de um minuto para conquistar um 'champion' interno no cliente, usando 'buy-in', 'to win over' e 'to align on'. O professor cronometra e pede uma versão mais persuasiva. Treina concisão.
lines: Start with: 'I'd love to have your support on this project because...'
Pitch de 60s para conquistar um champion interno no cliente. Vou cronometrar.
Required words: buy-in, to win over, to align on.
Peça uma versão mais persuasiva.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Como um champion salvou o projeto
practiceBank.how: O aluno narra uma história em que ganhar o apoio de um 'champion' destravou um projeto, usando 'gatekeeper', 'to keep informed' e 'common ground'. O professor pede uma sequência clara de eventos. Narrativa contínua.
lines: Start with: 'Let me tell you how one champion saved a project.'
Narre com sequência clara de eventos.
Use: gatekeeper, to keep informed, common ground.
(Peça:) What exactly did the champion do that unlocked it?
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Aluno vira o decision-maker
practiceBank.how: O aluno assume o papel do decision-maker do Google e o professor (Racional) tenta engajá-lo. O aluno responde no personagem, exigindo ser 'kept informed' e buscando 'common ground'. Treina vocabulário pela perspectiva inversa.

Cassio, I'd like to walk you through how we'll deliver this.
(Espere ele responder no personagem, exigindo ser kept informed.)
Use: to keep informed, common ground.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.how: O professor mostra um termo da aula e o aluno cria na hora uma frase sobre os stakeholders reais do shopping ('We need to win over the gatekeeper before the kickoff'). O professor corrige uso e pronúncia imediatamente.

Term: gatekeeper → (ex.: 'We need to win over the gatekeeper before the kickoff.')
Term: decision-maker → ?
Term: champion → ?
Term: common ground → ?

lessons.title: Executive presence & gravitas em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usará, em inglês simples, frases curtas e firmes para se posicionar com mais presença executiva.
lessons.overview:
Executive presence is the way you show up and speak in front of an important client. It is not about using difficult words in English; it is about being concise, composed and credible. For the Racional executive, this means conveying gravitas even in simple sentences.

In English, you don't need to speak fast. Learning to pause and to use phrases such as "My view is..." and "Let me be clear." helps you project confidence and come across as assured. When the client asks a difficult question, you can say "That's a fair question" and hold the line calmly.

With American clients, who value objectivity, this style is very effective. In this lesson you practice short sentences that show that Racional will not cut corners and that you know how to stand firm without losing your composure. Pause and clarity are worth more than many words.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "My view is clear.", "Let me be clear." e "That's a fair question."

Use pausas curtas entre as frases; isso ajuda a transmitir confiança.
lessons.situation: Em uma reunião tensa, um cliente da Amazon questiona o prazo da obra e você precisa responder com calma e firmeza.
lessons.context: Executive presence is about being calm and clear. I speak slowly. I pause. I keep my answers short. When a question is hard, I say: that's a fair question. My view is clear. We will not cut corners. I stand firm, but I stay polite.

vocab.example: Executive presence is about being calm.
He speaks with gravitas.
I pause before I answer.
I keep my answer concise.
I want to come across as calm.
She is always composed.
My view is clear.
Let me be clear about the plan.
I hold the line on quality.
We do not cut corners.
A clear answer is credible.
I project confidence with short sentences.
That's a fair question.
I stand firm, but I stay polite.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva
exercises.correctText: Let me be clear about the plan.
exercises.explanation: 'Let me be clear' é uma frase forte para se posicionar.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a melhor resposta
exercises.prompt: O cliente faz uma pergunta difícil. Qual resposta mostra calma e presença?

options.text: That's a fair question. My view is clear.
I don't know, sorry.
options.whyWrong: Não transmite confiança nem presença executiva.

options.text: Why do you ask me that?
options.whyWrong: Soa defensivo e pouco profissional.

exercises.title: 3. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: São qualidades da presença executiva.

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua resposta
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas para responder com firmeza a um cliente sobre qualidade. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula.
keywords: My view is|Let me be clear|fair question
exercises.modelAnswer: Let me be clear. We will not cut corners. My view is firm on quality.
exercises.explanation: Frases curtas e diretas transmitem mais confiança.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: That's a fair question. We will not cut corners.
exercises.translation: Essa é uma pergunta pertinente. Não vamos fazer de qualquer jeito.
exercises.prompt: Você responde com calma ao cliente da Amazon.
exercises.explanation: Faça uma pausa curta entre as duas frases.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15 a 20 segundos, responda com calma a um cliente que questiona o prazo: use 'fair question', uma pausa e uma frase firme.
takeaways: I can speak with executive presence in simple English.
I can pause and keep my answers concise.
I can say 'Let me be clear' and 'My view is...'.
I can stand firm and stay polite.

practiceBank.title: Responder com firmeza ao questionamento de prazo
practiceBank.how: O professor é o cliente da Amazon questionando o prazo da obra de forma tensa. O aluno responde com calma usando 'Let me be clear', 'My view is' e 'to hold the line'. O professor pressiona mais para testar a 'composure'. Treina presença executiva sob tensão.
lines: (Você é o cliente da Amazon, tenso.) Cássio, your team is behind schedule. The data center has to go live on time. What's going on?
That's not good enough. My leadership is asking me why Racional is slipping.
So you're telling me the date won't move? Be honest with me.
Other contractors would just add more people and push harder. Why won't you?
(Pressione mais.) I need a guarantee right now, Cássio. Can you give me one?
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Cadeira quente da reunião tensa
practiceBank.how: O aluno senta na cadeira quente e o professor dispara perguntas agressivas sobre atrasos e custos. O aluno responde de forma 'concise' e 'composed', usando 'fair question', 'to stand firm' e 'credible'. Treina manter a calma e a firmeza.
lines: You promised this slab by March. It's not done. Explain.
Your costs went up 12%. Who approved that?
Why should I trust Racional's numbers after this delay?
Are you cutting corners on quality to save time?
Give me one reason I shouldn't escalate this to your CEO.
(Deixe o aluno responder 'composed' e 'concise' a cada uma; corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: De frase longa para frase firme e curta
practiceBank.how: O professor diz uma resposta longa e hesitante e o aluno a reformula em frase curta e firme usando 'Let me be clear', 'My view is' e 'concise'. Vários estímulos em sequência. Treina concisão e gravitas.
lines: Long: 'Well, you know, I think that maybe, if everything goes okay, we could possibly try to hold the date, but I'm not totally sure.' → 'Let me be clear: we will hold the date.'
Long: 'Um, my opinion, sort of, is that we probably should not change the concrete mix at this point if possible.' → 'My view is: we don't change the concrete mix.'
Long: 'I'd say it's kind of important, in a way, to keep our usual quality standard on this build.' → 'Let me be clear: we will not cut corners on quality.'

practiceBank.title: Áudio se posicionando sobre o prazo
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60 segundos respondendo com firmeza por que o prazo será mantido, usando 'to hold the line', 'to project confidence' e 'composed'. Depois revisa o áudio com o professor focando em pausas e tom firme. Treina 'to pause' e ritmo.
lines: Start with: 'Let me be clear. We will hold the line on this delivery date.'
Target words to require: 'to hold the line', 'to project confidence', 'composed'.
Depois de gravar, toque o áudio e pergunte: Where could you pause to sound more composed?
Follow-up: Now say it again, slower, with one deliberate pause before 'hold the line'.

practiceBank.title: Falar com calma por 60s sem hesitar
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala um minuto inteiro defendendo a posição da Racional sem pausas longas nem 'um', usando 'composed', 'credible' e 'to project confidence'. O professor marca cada hesitação. Treina fluência e presença.
lines: Start with: 'My view is that Racional stands firm on quality, and here's why.'
Target words to require: 'composed', 'credible', 'to project confidence'.
Marque cada hesitação ('um', 'ah', pausa longa) com um tracinho no papel.
Follow-up: You hesitated 3 times. Run it again and beat that number.

practiceBank.title: Cliente diz que vão cortar custos
practiceBank.how: O professor insiste que a Racional deveria 'cut corners' para acelerar. O aluno se opõe com firmeza, usando 'Let me be clear', 'to hold the line' e 'credible'. O professor insiste de vários ângulos. Treina manter posição com gravitas.
lines: (Advogado do diabo.) Cássio, just cut a few corners on the finish, nobody at Amazon will notice.
Come on, every contractor does it under pressure. Why be different?
If you don't cut corners, you'll be late. Isn't a small shortcut better than a delay?
My boss only cares about the date, not the details. So why hold the line?
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Pausar com intenção
practiceBank.how: O professor dá frases curtas com gravitas e o aluno as repete inserindo pausas deliberadas ('Let me be clear... [pause] ...we will not cut corners'). Foco em 'to pause', entonação firme e clareza. Treina o impacto do silêncio.
lines: Repeat with a deliberate pause: 'Let me be clear... [pause] ...we will not cut corners.'
Repeat: 'My view is... [pause] ...we hold the line on quality.'
Repeat: 'That's a fair question... [pause] ...and here's my answer.'
Foco em 'to pause': o silêncio é parte da frase, não um erro.

practiceBank.title: Presença executiva é nata ou treinada?
practiceBank.how: O professor afirma 'Executive presence can't be learned'. O aluno discorda dando opinião com 'My view is' e justificando com 'to come across as', 'gravitas' e 'to project confidence'. O professor contra-argumenta para forçar produção.
lines: (Afirme provocando.) Executive presence can't be learned. You either have gravitas or you don't.
Look, some people just come across as credible, and the rest never will.
Training won't help you project confidence in front of a tough Amazon client.
(Force produção: peça 'My view is...' + um porquê com 'to come across as'.)
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Aluno vira o cliente tenso da Amazon
practiceBank.how: O aluno assume o papel do cliente irritado e o professor (Racional) responde com presença. Depois invertem. Ao viver os dois lados, o aluno percebe o efeito de 'composed', 'to stand firm' e 'fair question'. Treina o vocabulário pela perspectiva inversa.
lines: Now you are the angry Amazon client. Hit me with your toughest line about the delay.
(Responda como Racional, composed.) That's a fair question. Let me be clear...
Keep pushing me as the client. Don't let me off easy.
Now we switch back. Notice how 'composed' and 'to stand firm' felt from the client's side.
Follow-up: Which line made me, the client, calm down? Why?

practiceBank.title: Conte uma reunião onde manteve a posição
practiceBank.how: O aluno narra uma reunião difícil em que precisou 'stand firm', usando 'composed', 'to hold the line' e 'credible'. O professor pede que descreva como se sentiu e como reagiu. Narrativa contínua com vocabulário da aula.
lines: Tell me about a meeting where you had to hold the line. Set the scene first.
How did you stay composed when the client pushed?
What exactly did you say to stand firm?
How did the client react in the end?
Use 'credible', 'composed' and 'to hold the line' in your story.

practiceBank.title: Respostas firmes em rajada
practiceBank.how: O professor dispara provocações curtas ('You'll be late!', 'Cut the budget!') e o aluno rebate na hora com frases firmes ('Let me be clear...', 'That's a fair question, but...'). Ritmo rápido para automatizar respostas com gravitas.
lines: You'll be late!
Cut the budget!
Your quality is slipping!
Amazon is not happy!
Just add more workers!
Why should I trust Racional?

practiceBank.title: Cada expressão na resposta executiva
practiceBank.how: O professor mostra uma expressão da aula e o aluno a usa na hora numa resposta firme sobre a obra do shopping ('My view is we hold the line on quality'). O professor corrige tom, pausa e pronúncia imediatamente.
lines: Card: 'My view is' → use it in a firm answer about the shopping center build.
Card: 'to hold the line' → use it about a deadline with the client.
Card: 'credible' → use it about Racional's track record.
Card: 'fair question' → use it to open a tense answer.
Card: 'to cut corners' → use it to refuse a shortcut firmly.
(Corrija tom, pausa e pronúncia na hora, a cada card.)

leadIn: When a US client questions your timeline, how do you usually react?
What does 'executive presence' mean to you in a tense meeting?
Tell me about a time you had to stand firm with a client.
Why is it sometimes better to pause before answering a hard question?
Would Racional ever cut corners to deliver faster? Why or why not?

pill.tip: Em inglês, a sílaba tônica errada atrapalha a compreensão. "Record" como substantivo é REcord (tônica no início); como verbo é reCORD (tônica no fim).
pill.sample: Please record the meeting and save the record.

lessons.title: Storytelling de liderança
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue contar uma história curta de liderança em inglês — situação, desafio, virada e lição — para inspirar uma equipe ou um cliente.
lessons.overview:
Leaders don't convince with numbers alone; they convince with stories. Leadership storytelling is the art of telling a real case in a simple way: what happened, what the challenge was, what the turning point was, and what the lesson learned was. For a member of the Executive Board, this skill turns a cold report into a message that stays in people's minds.

In Racional's routine, you live stories like these all the time. Think of a project delivered against the odds, a hyperscale data center for Microsoft or Amazon that had to be ready on time even with unexpected events. When you tell this case to a North American client, you show more than technical competence: you show character, resilience, and the company's culture of more than 50 years and 620 projects.

The secret is the structure, not the difficult words. You open with a sentence to set the scene, present the problem, show the turning point, and close with the takeaway. In this lesson you build this script in simple English, with short sentences that any American executive understands and that make your message resonate.
lessons.intro:
Vamos relembrar três frases-âncora que sustentam qualquer história de liderança: "Here's what happened..." (para abrir), "Halfway through, we had a problem." (para o desafio) e "In the end, we delivered on time." (para o fechamento).

A ideia é simples: situar, mostrar o desafio, contar a virada e terminar com a lição. Frases curtas, no presente e no passado simples.
lessons.situation: Num jantar com um cliente norte-americano, ele pergunta sobre o projeto mais difícil da Racional. Você conta, em inglês simples, a história de uma obra entregue no prazo contra todas as probabilidades.
lessons.context: Here's what happened. We had a big project for a client. The deadline was very tight. Halfway through, we found a problem on site. It was hard, but the team did not give up. In the end, we delivered on time. The lesson was simple: a strong team can do great things together.

vocab.example: Good storytelling helps people remember your message.
First, I set the scene for the team.
The deadline was our biggest challenge.
That meeting was the turning point.

vocab.pt: Foi o seguinte / Veja o que aconteceu
vocab.example: Here's what happened on the project.
We took on a very hard job.
Halfway through, we found a problem.
The lesson learned was clear.
In the end, we did it.
We always try to deliver on time.
We finished against the odds.
A good story will resonate with the client.
My takeaway is simple: never give up.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Esses quatro termos formam a espinha de qualquer história de liderança.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase para abrir a história
exercises.prompt: Você quer começar a contar um caso para o cliente. Qual frase usar?

options.text: Here's what happened.
In the end, we delivered on time.
options.whyWrong: Essa é uma frase de fechamento, não de abertura.

options.text: The lesson learned was clear.
options.whyWrong: Essa frase serve para a lição final, não para abrir.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: We had a tight deadline, but ___ we delivered on time.
exercises.explanation: "In the end" introduz o resultado final da história.

exercises.title: 4. Conte uma mini-história
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases sobre um projeto difícil que deu certo. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula.
keywords: deliver on time|in the end|against the odds
exercises.modelAnswer: We had a big project with a tight deadline. The challenge was very hard. In the end, we delivered on time.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos da aula.

exercises.title: 5. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Here's what happened. The deadline was tight, but in the end, we delivered on time.
exercises.translation: Foi o seguinte. O prazo era apertado, mas no fim, entregamos no prazo.
exercises.prompt: Imagine que você está contando o caso para um cliente americano no jantar.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar e com pausas curtas para a história soar natural.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, conte em 15-20 segundos a história de um projeto difícil da Racional: abra com "Here's what happened", diga o desafio e feche com "In the end, we delivered on time".
takeaways: I can open a story with "Here's what happened".
I can talk about a challenge and a turning point.
I can close a story with "In the end".
I can share a simple lesson learned with a client.

Quebre a frase-alvo em blocos; o aluno encaixa e fala em voz alta, sem ler.
Aluno fala 90s sobre o tema; o professor faz perguntas no fim.
Aplique o alvo a uma situação real do projeto do aluno.

flow.what: Fechamento · O que eu aprendi nessa lição

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
