practiceBank.title: Recap da reunião de entrega
practiceBank.how: O aluno conta a um colega (professor) como foi a reunião de 'handover', do 'commissioning' ao 'sign off'. Narra no passado usando 'punch list', 'to wrap up', 'ready for occupancy'. Professor pede detalhes para esticar a fala.
lines: Você é o colega curioso. Diga: 'So how did the handover meeting go? Tell me from the start.'
Push for past tense: 'Did you finish the commissioning before the meeting?'
Ask: 'How many snags were left on the punch list?'
Ask: 'Did the client sign off, and did you wrap it all up?'

lessons.title: Site visit em inglês
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá conduzir uma visita ao canteiro em inglês, guiando o cliente e mostrando o andamento da obra.
lessons.overview:
The site visit (visita ao canteiro) is one of the most important moments in the client relationship. It's when the North American client walks through the project, sees the progress, and feels confident in the partner. For Racional, which builds offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers, guiding that visit naturally in English makes all the difference.

You will use short, practical guiding phrases: follow me (me siga), watch your step (cuidado com o degrau), this way (por aqui), and over here (aqui, deste lado). You will also point out parts of the project, such as the foundation (fundacao), the structure (estrutura), and each floor (andar/pavimento), as well as comment on the progress (andamento) and say that everything is on schedule (dentro do prazo).

This vocabulary turns a technical visit into a smooth conversation. When the client from Microsoft or Amazon walks through the data center and hears you explain each stage in simple English, they sense organization and command. This lesson prepares you to guide the visit from start to finish, with confidence and courtesy.
lessons.intro:
As frases-âncora desta aula são de guia: Please follow me. / Watch your step. / We are on schedule.

Use-as com gestos simples enquanto caminha com o cliente.
lessons.situation: Você guia um cliente norte-americano pela obra de um shopping center e mostra o andamento de cada andar.
lessons.context: Welcome to the site. Please put on your hard hat and your safety vest. Now, please follow me. Watch your step here. This way, please. Over here is the foundation. It is very strong. Now let's go up. This is the first floor. We are on schedule. The structure is ready. Let's take a look at the progress on this floor. Everything looks good. Let me walk you through the next area.

vocab.example: Thank you for the site visit.
Please put on your hard hat.
You need a safety vest here.
Please follow me.
Watch your step here.
Over here is the foundation.
The structure is ready.
We are on schedule.
Let's look at the progress.
Let me walk you through this area.
Over here is the main entrance.
This is the first floor.
Let's take a look at this room.
This way, please.

exercises.title: 1. Associe o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: Termos básicos para guiar uma visita ao canteiro.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva o convite
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases curtas para começar a guiar o cliente pela obra. Use pelo menos 2 termos da aula (por exemplo: follow me, hard hat, this way).
exercises.modelAnswer: Please put on your hard hat and follow me. This way, please, and watch your step.
exercises.explanation: A correção foca só no uso dos termos de guia; mantenha tudo curto.

exercises.title: 3. Escolha a frase de guia
exercises.prompt: Você quer pedir que o cliente caminhe atrás de você. O que você diz?

options.text: Please follow me.
Please follow you.
options.whyWrong: "Follow you" significa seguir o próprio cliente; o correto é "follow me".

options.text: Please stay here.
options.whyWrong: Isso pede que ele fique parado, não que caminhe com você.

exercises.title: 4. Coloque na ordem certa
exercises.explanation: Frase simples no presente para dizer que a obra está no prazo.

exercises.title: 5. Fale em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Please follow me. Watch your step. We are on schedule.
exercises.translation: Por favor, me siga. Cuidado com o degrau. Estamos dentro do prazo.
exercises.prompt: Você está guiando o cliente entre dois andares. Diga estas frases enquanto caminha.
exercises.explanation: Fale de forma clara e cordial, como um bom anfitrião.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, por cerca de 15 a 20 segundos, guie um cliente pela obra: dê as boas-vindas, peça que use capacete e colete, peça que o siga, avise sobre o degrau e diga que a obra está no prazo.
takeaways: I can welcome a client to the site.
I can ask a client to wear a hard hat and follow me.
I can say watch your step and this way.
I can say we are on schedule.
I can walk a client through the site.

practiceBank.title: Guiando o cliente pelos andares do shopping
practiceBank.how: O aluno guia o cliente americano pela obra do shopping center andar por andar, usando 'this way', 'over here', 'watch your step' e 'to walk through'. Deve mostrar o 'progress' de cada 'floor'. Professor faz o cliente que para e pergunta sobre cada nível.

Prompt as he guides: 'What's the progress on this floor?'
Ask: 'Is the structure done here, or still in progress?'

(O aluno usa this way / over here / watch your step / to walk through. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Planta de andares e andamento
practiceBank.how: O professor mostra um corte do shopping center com vários 'floors'. O aluno descreve o que está pronto em cada nível ('foundation', 'structure', 'to be on schedule'). Produz frases de guia como 'Over here we have the structure done'. Professor pede comparações entre andares.

practiceBank.how: O aluno simula caminhar pela obra narrando em tempo real ('Follow me', 'Watch your step', 'Let's take a look at the structure'). Deve manter a narração contínua por dois minutos. Professor caminha junto fazendo perguntas pontuais sobre o 'progress'.

Caminhe junto e pergunte: 'What about the progress on this level?'
Prompt if he stops: 'Keep going, take me to the next floor.'
(Narração contínua por dois minutos. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Tour em áudio do andar térreo
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60s guiando o cliente pelo térreo do shopping, usando 'site visit', 'hard hat', 'safety vest', 'over here'. Deve soar como um guia natural. Professor ouve e dá feedback de fluidez e expressões de orientação.
lines: Diga: 'Record 60 seconds guiding the client through the ground floor of the mall.'
Start with: 'Welcome to the site. First, please put on your hard hat and safety vest...'
Require: site visit, hard hat, safety vest, over here.
Depois ouça e pergunte: 'Repeat the part where you point something out with over here.'
(Feedback de fluidez e expressões de orientação.)

practiceBank.title: Qual andar está em qual fase
practiceBank.how: Aluno e professor têm informações diferentes sobre o status de cada 'floor'. Conversando, descobrem qual nível está em 'foundation', 'structure' ou 'on schedule'. O aluno faz perguntas e descreve até completar o quadro. Sem mostrar os papéis.

Ask: 'Which floor has the structure done?'
Prompt: 'Which levels are on schedule on your side?'
Close: 'Okay, let's confirm the full picture, floor by floor.'
(O aluno faz perguntas e descreve até completar o quadro.)

practiceBank.title: Comando de guia relâmpago
practiceBank.how: O professor aponta uma situação (degrau, capacete faltando, próximo andar) e o aluno reage com a expressão certa ('Watch your step', 'You need a hard hat', 'This way'). Rodada rápida cobrindo todas as frases de condução. Foco em reação espontânea.
lines: Aponte uma situação e peça a reação certa. Diga: 'There's a step right in front of the client.' → expect 'Watch your step.'
'The client has no helmet.' → expect 'You need a hard hat.'
'You want to move to the next floor.' → expect 'This way, please.'
'You want to point out a finished column.' → expect 'Over here we have...'
(Rodada rápida. Foco em reação espontânea.)

practiceBank.title: Antes e depois da obra
practiceBank.how: Duas imagens do mesmo andar (início vs. atual). O aluno descreve as diferenças de 'progress', falando sobre 'foundation' e 'structure'. Produz frases comparativas e confirma se está 'on schedule'. Professor faz perguntas sobre o que mudou.
lines: Mostre duas imagens do mesmo andar, início vs atual. Diga: 'Tell me what changed between these two.'
Ask: 'What progress do you see on the structure now?'
Ask: 'Was this level at foundation stage before?'
Ask: 'Based on this, is this floor on schedule?'
(Frases comparativas. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Cliente pergunta sobre prazos
practiceBank.how: Troca rápida: professor pergunta 'Is this floor on schedule?', 'When will the structure be done?' e o aluno responde em uma frase. Depois inverte. Ritmo veloz para fixar 'progress', 'to be on schedule', 'floor'.
lines: Is this floor on schedule?
When will the structure be done?
What's the progress on the ground floor?
Is the foundation finished on this level?
How many floors are we walking through today?
Which floor is the most advanced?
Agora inverta: peça ao aluno que faça as perguntas. (Ritmo veloz.)

practiceBank.title: Cliente quer ver área não liberada
practiceBank.how: O cliente (professor) pede para entrar numa área ainda em 'structure', sem segurança. O aluno desvia educadamente, oferece outro ponto ('Let's take a look at the floor over here') e explica o motivo. Deve combinar guia e segurança no discurso.
lines: Você é o cliente. Diga: 'I'd like to go into that area over there, the one still under structure.'
Push: 'Come on, just for a minute, I want to see it up close.'
Listen as he redirects, then: 'Why can't I go in there?'
Accept the alternative: 'Okay, what can you show me instead?'
(O aluno combina guia e segurança. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Aluno é o cliente curioso
practiceBank.how: Os papéis se invertem: o aluno faz o cliente que questiona tudo durante o 'site visit', e o professor guia. Depois trocam de novo, e o aluno repete o tour incorporando as boas perguntas que ouviu. Foco em ouvir e reusar expressões de guia.
lines: Inverta os papéis. Diga: 'Now you're the curious client. Question everything during the site visit, and I'll guide.'
Como guia, dê deixas: 'This way, please, watch your step.'
Depois troque de volta: 'Okay, now you guide again, and use the good questions you just heard.'
Ask: 'Show me the progress on this floor as the guide now.'
(Foco em ouvir e reusar expressões de guia.)

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sem parar sobre o andamento

lines: Diga: 'Speak for one full minute, no long pauses, describing the progress of the mall.'
Start with: 'Right now, the project is on schedule, and over here...'
Require: on schedule, structure, walk through.
Sinalize quando travar: 'Keep going, take me to the next floor.'

practiceBank.title: Recap do tour para o chefe
practiceBank.how: O aluno conta ao chefe (professor) como foi a 'site visit' com o cliente, narrando o que mostrou em cada andar. Usa no passado 'to walk through', 'watch your step', 'on schedule'. Professor pede detalhes de cada nível para esticar a fala.
lines: Você é o chefe. Diga: 'So how was the site visit with the client? Tell me what you showed him on each floor.'
Push for past tense: 'Did you walk him through every level?'
Ask: 'Did you remind him to watch his step?'
Ask: 'Was everything on schedule when you showed it?'
(Narração no passado. Peça detalhes de cada nível.)

lessons.title: Personal hobbies & sports (cycling, swimming, walking)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá conversar sobre hobbies e esportes em inglês simples, criando conexão com o cliente fora das reuniões.
lessons.overview:
Not every important conversation happens in the meeting room. With North American clients, small talk (conversa informal) about hobbies (hobbies) and sports creates real rapport. In a project cycle of 18 to 24 months, these light moments between site work and dinners help build a long-term relationship of trust.

This lesson brings simple vocabulary to talk about activities like cycling (ciclismo), swimming (natacao), and hiking. You will learn useful expressions such as to be into something (curtir/gostar muito de algo), to work out (treinar/se exercitar), to stay active (manter-se ativo), and to clear my head (espairecer). These are short phrases that sound natural over coffee or in the car on the way to the site.

Americans often appreciate people who take care of their health and keep an active routine. Knowing how to say what you like to do on weekends, or asking about the client's favorite sport, opens doors and humanizes the relationship. Here the focus is not heavy grammar, but genuine connection in simple English.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta conversa: I'm into cycling. / I work out to stay active. / What do you do to unwind?

Use-as com tom leve, como numa conversa de café.
lessons.situation: Depois de uma reunião, você toma um café com o cliente norte-americano e conversa sobre esportes e fim de semana.
lessons.context: On the weekend, I like to stay active. I'm into cycling. I ride my bike for one hour. I also like swimming. It helps me clear my head. Sometimes I just go for a walk outdoors. It is a nice way to unwind after a busy week. I try to work out three times a week. It keeps me fit. What about you? What do you do to relax on the weekend?

vocab.example: Cycling is my favorite hobby.
I'm into cycling.
I work out three times a week.
I like to stay active.
I enjoy cycling on Sundays.
Swimming is good for me.
I go for a walk every morning.
A walk helps me clear my head.
I cycle to unwind.
I like to be outdoors.

I walk to keep fit.
I run at an easy pace.

lessons.title: Sustainability & green building (LEED)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre construção sustentável e certificação LEED em inglês simples, conectando o tema ao valor do projeto.
lessons.overview:
Sustainable construction is now a central criterion for North American clients. Companies like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google have carbon targets and want partners who deliver green buildings. For Racional, talking about sustainability (sustentabilidade) and green building (construcao verde) in English shows that the company is aligned with the global agenda.

This lesson brings the vocabulary of the topic: the LEED certification (certificacao LEED), energy-efficient (eficientes em energia) buildings, reducing the carbon footprint (pegada de carbono), the use of renewable energy (energia renovavel) and low-carbon materials (materiais de baixo carbono). You will also connect this to the business: green buildings lower operating costs (custos de operacao) and raise asset value (valor do ativo).

For a board-level executive, this is a strategic message. Showing the client that the investment in sustainability pays off (se paga, da retorno) over time connects the technical topic to ROI. This lesson gives you simple phrases to defend that value in a conversation with the American client.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: Our building is energy-efficient. / We use renewable energy. / Green building pays off over time.

São frases curtas que ligam sustentabilidade a valor.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a um cliente norte-americano por que o novo escritório será uma construção verde com certificação LEED.
lessons.context: Sustainability is very important to us. This new office is a green building. It will have LEED certification. The building is energy-efficient. We use renewable energy, like solar power. We also use low-carbon materials. This reduces the carbon footprint. A green building has lower operating costs. It also has a higher asset value. In the end, green building pays off over time. It is good for the planet and good for business.

lessons.title: BIM & construction tech
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conseguirá falar sobre BIM e tecnologia de construção em inglês simples, explicando seus benefícios ao cliente.
lessons.overview:
Technology has changed the way we build. The digital model (modelo digital), known as BIM, is now at the heart of large projects. For North American clients in data centers and hospitals, seeing that Racional uses a single source of truth (uma unica fonte de verdade) with all the project's data conveys trust and modernity.

In this lesson you will talk about tools that are easy to explain: clash detection (deteccao de conflitos entre projetos), the coordination of the MEP disciplines (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing), 4D scheduling (cronograma em 4D, linking the model to time), and the drone survey (levantamento por drone). You will also see prefabrication (pre-fabricacao) and modular construction (construcao modular), which speed up the work.

The core benefit is clear: technology helps you flag a conflict (apontar um conflito) before construction begins, avoiding the do-over (retrabalho). For an executive, that means less risk, lower cost, and deadlines met. This lesson gives you simple phrases to show the client how technology protects the project.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora desta aula: We use a digital model. / It is our single source of truth. / We find conflicts before we build.

Frases curtas que mostram o valor da tecnologia.
lessons.situation: Você apresenta a um cliente norte-americano como a Racional usa BIM e tecnologia para reduzir risco no projeto de um data center.
lessons.context: We use a lot of technology in our projects. First, we build a digital model. This model is our single source of truth. All the teams use the same data. We use clash detection to find conflicts early. For example, we check the MEP systems. If we find a conflict, we flag it before we build. This saves time and money. We also use drone survey to check the progress. And we use prefabrication to build faster. Technology helps us reduce risk.

vocab.example: We build a digital model.
We use clash detection.
The model is our single source of truth.
We check the MEP systems.
We update the as-built model.
Design coordination is important.
Good planning avoids a do-over.

We use a drone survey.
Prefabrication helps us build faster.
We use modular construction.
The model integrates all disciplines.
We flag a conflict before we build.

lines: Você é o cliente americano. Diga: 'Show me how Racional uses BIM to reduce risk on the data center.'
Ask: 'What do you mean by single source of truth?'
Push: 'How does this actually avoid rework?'
Ask: 'Walk me through how you flag a conflict before building.'
(Produção encadeada com o vocab. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Explicando uma clash detection
practiceBank.how: O professor mostra um print de um modelo 3D com uma colisão MEP. O aluno explica a 'clash detection', aponta o conflito e diz como o BIM evita o 'do-over'. Produz frases técnicas simples usando 'to integrate disciplines'. Professor pede que detalhe o impacto.
lines: Mostre um print de modelo 3D com uma colisão MEP. Diga: 'Explain this clash detection to me.'
Ask: 'Where exactly is the conflict, and what disciplines collide?'
Ask: 'How does catching this in the model avoid a do-over?'
Ask: 'How does BIM integrate the disciplines here?'
(Frases técnicas simples. Peça que detalhe o impacto.)

practiceBank.title: BIM em 45s
practiceBank.how: O aluno faz um pitch curto convencendo o cliente de que o 'digital model' é o 'single source of truth' do projeto. Deve mencionar 'clash detection', 'design coordination' e 'as-built' em 45 segundos. Professor cronometra e cobra concisão.
lines: Diga: 'You have 45 seconds. Pitch BIM as the single source of truth to the client.'
Start with: 'Our digital model is the single source of truth, which means...'
Require: clash detection, design coordination, as-built.
Cronometre e ao final: 'That ran over. Tighten it to 45 seconds.'
(Cobra concisão.)

practiceBank.title: Dúvidas sobre a tecnologia
practiceBank.how: Troca rápida: professor pergunta sobre 'drone survey', '4D scheduling', 'prefabrication' e o aluno responde em uma frase. Depois inverte os papéis. Ritmo veloz para fixar o vocab de tecnologia de construção.
lines: What is a drone survey used for?
What does 4D scheduling add to a project?
How does prefabrication speed things up?
What's the level of detail in your model?
What is an as-built model?
How does modular construction reduce risk?
Agora inverta: peça ao aluno que faça as perguntas. (Ritmo veloz.)

practiceBank.title: Conflito MEP detectado tarde
practiceBank.how: Surge um 'clash' entre dutos e tubulação (MEP) já em campo. O aluno explica ao cliente como o BIM teria 'flagged the conflict' antes e como evitar o 'do-over'. Deve manter o tom de solução usando 'design coordination'. Professor pressiona como cliente preocupado.
lines: Crie o cenário: 'There's a clash between ducts and piping, MEP, and it was found in the field. Explain it.'
Push: 'Why wasn't this flagged earlier?'
Listen, then: 'How would BIM have flagged this conflict before we built?'
Ask: 'How do we avoid the do-over now?'
(Mantém o tom de solução. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Como o BIM reduz risco
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60s explicando ao cliente como BIM e 'modular construction' reduzem risco no data center. Deve usar 'digital model', 'clash detection', 'prefabrication', 'to flag a conflict'. Professor ouve e dá feedback de clareza técnica.
lines: Diga: 'Record 60 seconds explaining how BIM and modular construction reduce risk on the data center.'
Start with: 'BIM reduces risk because the digital model lets us...'
Require: digital model, clash detection, prefabrication, to flag a conflict.
Depois ouça e pergunte: 'Repeat the part about flagging a conflict.'
(Feedback de clareza técnica.)

practiceBank.title: Prefabrication vs. construção no local
practiceBank.how: O aluno defende 'prefabrication' e 'modular construction' contra o método tradicional, usando 'do-over', '4D scheduling', 'design coordination'. Professor faz o advogado do diabo defendendo o convencional. Foco em argumentar com justificativa.
lines: Você é o advogado do diabo. Diga: 'Traditional on-site construction is proven. Why switch to prefabrication?'
Push: 'Modular feels risky to me. Convince me.'
Ask: 'How does it cut down on do-overs?'
Ask: 'How does 4D scheduling help with prefabrication?'
(Foco em argumentar com justificativa. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Status das disciplinas no modelo
practiceBank.how: Aluno e professor têm dados diferentes sobre o 'level of detail' de cada disciplina (MEP, estrutura). Conversando, descobrem onde há 'clash' e o que falta 'to integrate'. O aluno faz perguntas e descreve até completar o quadro. Sem mostrar os papéis.
lines: Explique: vocês têm dados diferentes sobre o level of detail de cada disciplina. Não mostrem os papéis.
Ask: 'On my side, structure is at LOD 300. What about MEP on yours?'
Ask: 'Where do you see a clash between disciplines?'
Prompt: 'What still needs to be integrated?'
Close: 'Let's confirm the full status across all disciplines.'
(O aluno faz perguntas e descreve até completar o quadro.)

practiceBank.title: Frase relâmpago de tech
practiceBank.how: O professor sorteia um termo ('drone survey', 'as-built', 'single source of truth') e o aluno faz uma frase imediata ligada ao data center. Rodada rápida cobrindo todo o vocab. Foco em uso correto e ágil.
lines: Sorteie um termo e peça uma frase ligada ao data center. Diga: 'Make a sentence with: drone survey.'
Then: 'Now with: as-built.'
Then: 'Now with: single source of truth.'
Then: 'Now with: to flag a conflict.'
(Foco em uso correto e ágil.)

practiceBank.title: Aluno é o cliente cético
practiceBank.how: O aluno assume o papel do cliente americano cético sobre o custo do BIM e questiona o professor. Depois trocam: o aluno responde às próprias objeções usando 'to flag a conflict', 'do-over', 'design coordination'. Foco em antecipar e rebater dúvidas.
lines: Inverta os papéis. Diga: 'You're the skeptical US client. Question me about the cost of BIM.'
Responda de forma incompleta para ele cobrar.
Depois troque: 'Now you answer your own objections.'
Ask: 'How do you justify BIM with to flag a conflict and avoiding a do-over?'
(Foco em antecipar e rebater dúvidas.)

practiceBank.title: Especialista de BIM no banquinho
practiceBank.how: O aluno é o especialista de BIM e responde a uma rajada de perguntas do cliente: 'How does clash detection work?', 'What is 4D scheduling?'. Não pode travar; usa o vocab técnico. Professor mantém o ritmo alto.
lines: How does clash detection work?
What is 4D scheduling?
Why is the model the single source of truth?
How does a drone survey help you?
What's the difference between the design model and the as-built?
How does design coordination prevent a do-over?
(Rajada de perguntas. Ele não pode travar; corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Como o BIM salvou o projeto
practiceBank.how: O aluno narra um caso em que a 'clash detection' evitou um 'do-over' caro no data center. Conta a história no passado usando 'to flag a conflict', 'design coordination', 'single source of truth'. Professor pede detalhes para esticar a narração.
lines: Diga: 'Tell me a story where clash detection saved the project from a costly do-over.'
Start with: 'On one data center, the model flagged a conflict that...'
Require past tense and: to flag a conflict, design coordination, single source of truth.
Ask: 'How much rework did that save?'
(Narração no passado. Peça detalhes para esticar a fala.)

leadIn: What is a digital model, in simple words?
Why is the model called the single source of truth?
Can you explain clash detection to a non-technical client?
How does BIM help you find conflicts before you build?
How do you use drone surveys on a data center project?

lessons.title: Subcontractor management
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você fala sobre gestão de subcontratados em inglês simples — como a Racional escolhe, integra e acompanha seus parceiros de obra — numa conversa com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
No Racional project is built by Racional alone. On a hyperscale data center for Microsoft or a large hospital, dozens of specialized companies work together: electrical, HVAC, foundations, facade. Each one is a subcontractor (subcontratado), responsible for a trade (especialidade tecnica). Knowing how to talk about this chain in English is essential, because the American client wants to understand who does what and how quality is guaranteed.

The cycle begins long before the site. Racional needs to pre-qualify (pre-qualificar) and to vet (avaliar/checar) each company before hiring, then carry out the scope handoff (passagem de escopo) clearly. During the work, the site supervisor (supervisor de campo) keeps everyone to a standard (no padrao) and manages the interface (interface/conexao) between teams. At the end of each stage, a snag list (lista de pendencias) records what still needs to be fixed.

For a Racional Board executive, this vocabulary communicates governance and risk control. When you say, in clear English, that the company pre-qualifies suppliers and that a supervisor is accountable for the result - to own the outcome (assumir o resultado) - the American client senses process maturity. That's what sustains 18- to 24-month relationships with key accounts.
lessons.intro:
Vamos praticar três estruturas-âncora simples: "We pre-qualify every subcontractor.", "The site supervisor coordinates all trades." e "We hold them to one standard."

Repita essas frases em voz alta. Elas serão a base da sua conversa de hoje.
lessons.situation: Numa site visit, um cliente americano pergunta como a Racional controla a qualidade das empresas que trabalham na obra. Você explica o processo, do começo ao fim.
lessons.context: We do not build alone. On a big project, many companies work with us. Each company has one trade. Before we hire, we pre-qualify and vet them. Then we do a clear scope handoff. On site, the site supervisor coordinates all the trades. He holds every team to one standard. At the end of each stage, we make a snag list. We fix the small problems on the list. We own the outcome. The client trusts our process.

vocab.example: Each subcontractor has one job on site.
Electrical work is one trade.
We pre-qualify every company before we hire.
We vet the vendor first.
A clear scope handoff stops problems.
The site supervisor is on site every day.
He coordinates all the teams.
The interface between two trades is important.
We fix the snag list before we finish.
We hold every team to one standard.
This vendor is fast and safe.
We supervise the work every day.
We own the outcome of the project.

exercises.title: 1. Ligue o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: São quatro termos-chave da gestão de subcontratados na obra.

exercises.title: 2. Escolha a frase correta

options.text: We pre-qualify and vet every company.

exercises.title: 3. Complete a frase

exercises.title: 4. Escreva sua resposta

exercises.explanation: Frase-âncora que transmite governança ao cliente americano.

practiceBank.title: Site visit: "Como vocês controlam a qualidade?"
practiceBank.how: O professor é o cliente americano do shopping center numa site visit e pergunta como a Racional escolhe e acompanha os subcontratados. O aluno explica o processo do começo ao fim usando 'to pre-qualify', 'to vet', 'site supervisor', 'to own the outcome'. Professor interrompe com perguntas de aprofundamento.
lines: Você é o cliente americano na site visit. Diga: 'How does Racional choose and control its subcontractors? Walk me through it.'
Interrompa: 'You said you pre-qualify them. What does that actually involve?'
Push: 'And how do you vet a new vendor?'
Ask: 'Who's the site supervisor, and how do you own the outcome?'
(O aluno explica do começo ao fim. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: A jornada de um subcontratado de fachada
practiceBank.how: O aluno narra, em voz alta e em primeira pessoa, todo o ciclo de um 'trade' de fachada do mall: como foi feito o 'pre-qualify', o 'scope handoff', a 'supervise' e a 'snag list' final. Professor anota o vocab usado e devolve os termos que faltaram.
lines: Diga: 'Tell me the full story of a facade trade on the mall, in the first person, out loud.'
Prompt: 'Start with how you pre-qualified them.'
Ask: 'How did the scope handoff go?'
Ask: 'How did you supervise the work and handle the final snag list?'
(Anote o vocab usado e devolva os termos que faltaram no final.)

practiceBank.title: Dois subcontratados, uma decisão
practiceBank.how: Professor entrega ao aluno só metade dos dados de dois 'vendors' (um tem melhor 'standard', outro melhor preço) e guarda a outra metade. O aluno faz perguntas para completar e recomenda quem 'pre-qualify', justificando com o vocab. Professor responde só ao que for perguntado.
lines: Explique: você tem só metade dos dados de dois vendors. Não mostre o papel.
Diga: 'I have two vendors here. Ask me questions to fill in what you're missing.'
Responda só ao que for perguntado: 'Vendor A has a higher standard, Vendor B is cheaper.'
Prompt: 'So, which one do you pre-qualify, and why?'
(O aluno faz perguntas para completar e recomenda, justificando com o vocab.)

practiceBank.title: Cadeia o termo certo
practiceBank.how: Professor descreve uma situação de obra do shopping ('o supervisor achou um defeito no acabamento') e o aluno responde usando o termo-alvo exato ('snag list', 'site supervisor'). Ritmo rápido, sem traduzir; professor só dá a deixa.
lines: Descreva uma situação e peça o termo-alvo exato. Diga: 'The supervisor found a defect in the finishing. What do you do?' → expect 'Add it to the snag list.'
'Who walks the site every day checking the work?' → expect 'The site supervisor.'
'You're passing the work package to the electrician.' → expect 'That's the scope handoff.'
'You promise the client the result is on you.' → expect 'We own the outcome.'
(Ritmo rápido, sem traduzir; só dê a deixa.)

practiceBank.title: Defenda seu processo de vetting
practiceBank.how: O aluno está na 'hot seat' como gerente da Racional; professor e (imaginariamente) o cliente disparam perguntas céticas sobre 'how do you vet?', 'who owns the outcome?'. Aluno responde sem pausas longas, sustentando o discurso com o vocab da aula.
lines: Você é o cliente cético na hot seat dele. Dispare: 'How do you vet a subcontractor?'
'Who owns the outcome if a trade fails?'
'How do you pre-qualify before signing?'
'What stops a bad vendor from getting on my site?'
(Aluno responde sem pausas longas, sustentando com o vocab. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: O que mais garante qualidade?
practiceBank.how: Professor lista 5 práticas (pre-qualify, vet, site supervision, scope handoff claro, snag list). O aluno ordena da mais à menos importante para o shopping e justifica cada posição em inglês. Professor joga o advogado do diabo em 1-2 escolhas.
lines: Liste 5 práticas: pre-qualify, vet, site supervision, clear scope handoff, snag list. Diga: 'Rank these from most to least important for the mall, and justify each.'
Ask: 'Why is your number one the strongest guarantee of quality?'
Como advogado do diabo: 'I'd put snag list first. Convince me you're right.'
Question another: 'Is the scope handoff really that important?'
(O aluno justifica cada posição em inglês.)

practiceBank.title: Coordenação entre trades
practiceBank.how: Reunião curta onde o aluno coordena dois 'trades' que se chocam no cronograma (elétrica x gesso) no mall. Ele usa 'to coordinate', 'interface', 'to supervise' para resolver o conflito. Professor faz o papel de um dos subcontratados resistente.
lines: Você é um subcontratado resistente. Diga: 'My electrical crew can't work while the drywall guys are in there. It's their problem, not mine.'
Push: 'Why should I change my schedule?'
Ouça como ele coordena, então: 'Fine, but who manages the interface between us?'
Ask: 'And who supervises that this actually works?'
(O aluno usa to coordinate, interface, to supervise. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Pergunta e devolve sobre vendors
practiceBank.how: Aluno e professor alternam perguntas rápidas sobre gestão de subcontratados ('Who do you pre-qualify first?', 'What's a snag list?'). Cada um deve responder e logo lançar a próxima, mantendo o vocab vivo. Professor sobe o ritmo gradualmente.

What's a snag list?

Agora inverta: peça ao aluno que lance as perguntas e suba o ritmo. (Mantém o vocab vivo.)

practiceBank.title: O fluxo do scope handoff
practiceBank.how: Professor mostra (ou desenha) um fluxo simples: contrato → scope handoff → supervisão → snag list. O aluno descreve cada etapa em voz alta como se explicasse ao cliente americano. Professor pede para ele 'own' cada etapa com clareza.
lines: Desenhe ou mostre o fluxo: contract → scope handoff → supervision → snag list. Diga: 'Describe each step out loud as if you're explaining it to the US client.'
Ask: 'What happens at the scope handoff exactly?'
Ask: 'Who supervises after the handoff?'
Push: 'Own each step clearly, tell me Racional is responsible for the result.'
(O aluno descreve cada etapa. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Subcontratado abaixo do standard
practiceBank.how: Cenário: um 'subcontractor' está entregando abaixo do 'standard' no shopping e o cliente notou. O aluno explica, falando, como a Racional vai 'supervise', corrigir e 'own the outcome'. Professor pressiona com 'and if it happens again?'.

Ask: 'How will you supervise to fix it?'
Push: 'And if it happens again?'
Ask: 'Who owns the outcome here, you or the vendor?'
(O aluno fala como vai corrigir e own the outcome. Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Pitch de 60s: nosso modelo de subcontratação
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava 60 segundos explicando ao cliente como a Racional gerencia subcontratados de ponta a ponta, usando ao menos 6 termos da aula. Depois ouve a própria gravação e o professor aponta 1 ganho e 1 ajuste.
lines: Diga: 'Record 60 seconds explaining how Racional manages subcontractors end to end.'
Start with: 'At Racional, we manage subcontractors from start to finish. First, we pre-qualify...'
Require at least 6 terms: subcontractor, to pre-qualify, to vet, scope handoff, site supervisor, to own the outcome.
Depois ouça com ele e aponte 1 ganho e 1 ajuste.
(Avalie clareza e uso do vocab.)

practiceBank.title: O aluno vira o cliente exigente
practiceBank.how: Inverte-se: o aluno faz o cliente americano do mall e formula as perguntas mais difíceis sobre vetting e qualidade; o professor responde de forma incompleta de propósito. O aluno deve cobrar detalhes usando o vocab. Bom para ouvir o termo do outro lado.
lines: Inverta os papéis: o aluno é o cliente exigente do mall. Diga: 'You're the client now. Ask me the hardest questions about vetting and quality.'
Responda de propósito de forma incompleta: 'We just pick good companies, that's all.'
Force-o a cobrar: deixe-o pedir detalhes usando o vocab.
Prompt: 'Push me on who owns the outcome and how we vet.'
(Bom para ouvir o termo do outro lado.)

practiceBank.title: Um minuto sobre 'to own the outcome'
practiceBank.how: O aluno fala sem parar por 1 minuto sobre o que significa 'own the outcome' na gestão de subcontratados da Racional, sem repetir-se nem parar. Professor cronometra e marca quando o aluno trava, retomando depois.
lines: Diga: 'Speak for one full minute, non-stop, on what it means to own the outcome in subcontractor management at Racional.'
Start with: 'To own the outcome means that, no matter who does the work...'
Cronometre e marque quando travar, retomando depois.
Sinalize: 'Keep going, give me a concrete example from the mall.'
(Sem repetir-se nem parar.)

lessons.title: Meeting fundamentals: agenda, minutes, action items
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a estrutura de uma reunião em inglês simples — define a pauta, registra as decisões e distribui os action items — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Well-run meetings are the heart of Module 4. In monthly and biweekly meetings with clients like Amazon or Google, Racional needs to show that it controls both time and decisions. It all starts with the agenda (pauta): a clear list of agenda items (itens de pauta) that keeps everyone focused and respects an executive's packed schedule.

During the meeting, someone needs to take minutes (registrar a ata) - to note what was decided. Each decision becomes an action item (item de acao) with an owner (responsavel) and a due date (prazo). If a topic doesn't fit right now, you can to park (deixar de lado) it and send it to the parking lot (lista de pendencias para depois), without wasting the meeting's time.

The American client values punctuality and clarity. When you keep everyone to time (mantem todos no horario) and then send a recap email (e-mail de resumo) with who does what and by when - by end of day (ate o fim do dia), for example - you project the governance that the Racional Board represents. That's how meetings turn into real action.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora de hoje: "Let's start with the agenda.", "I'll take the minutes." e "Each action item has an owner and a due date."

Repita-as. Elas estruturam qualquer reunião em inglês.
lessons.situation: Você abre uma reunião quinzenal com o cliente americano. Precisa definir a pauta, controlar o tempo e fechar com os action items claros.
lessons.context: Let's start with the agenda. We have three agenda items today. I will take the minutes. For each decision, we set an action item. Every action item has an owner and a due date. Please keep us to time. If a topic is too big now, we park it. We put it in the parking lot for later. After the meeting, I send a recap email. The email lists who does what and by when. This way, the meeting turns into action.

vocab.example: We have three items on the agenda.
The first agenda item is the budget.
I send the minutes after the meeting.
I will take the minutes today.
Each action item has an owner.
Who is the owner of this task?
The due date is Friday.
Please keep us to time.
Let's park this topic for now.
We put it in the parking lot.
I send a recap email today.
I assign this task to John.
Please send it by end of day.

Let's take the minutes of this.

I can say I will take the minutes.
I can give each action item an owner and a due date.
I can park a topic and send a recap email.

practiceBank.title: Abre a quinzenal do shopping
practiceBank.how: O aluno abre uma reunião quinzenal com o cliente americano: anuncia a 'agenda', conduz os 'agenda items' e fecha com 'action items'. Professor faz o cliente que tenta sair do tema, e o aluno usa 'to park' e 'parking lot' para controlar.
lines: Open the biweekly meeting. Start with: 'Good morning, thanks for joining. Here's the agenda for today.'
List three agenda items out loud for the shopping center project.
Eu vou tentar fugir da pauta falando de custos extras — você usa 'parking lot' para me conter.
Pressure: 'But wait, can we talk about the budget right now?' — você responde com 'let's park that'.
Close by assigning one action item with an owner and a due date.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Distribuindo action items
practiceBank.how: Ao fim de uma reunião sobre atrasos no mall, o aluno atribui tarefas: 'action item', 'owner', 'due date', 'by end of day'. Professor é um participante que pede prazo maior e o aluno renegocia mantendo clareza.
lines: Assign the first action item: who is the owner and what's the due date?
Eu peço mais prazo: 'Can I get an extra week on that?' — você renegocia mantendo clareza.
Pressure: 'End of day is too tight, honestly.' — você responde sem perder o controle.
Confirm: 'So the owner is ___ and it's due by end of day Friday, agreed?'
Re-assign a second action item to a different owner with a new due date.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Reconstrua a ata
practiceBank.how: Professor lê duas vezes um curto resumo de reunião com decisões e prazos do shopping. O aluno reconstrói a 'minutes' em voz alta usando 'to take minutes', 'owner', 'due date'. Compara com o original e ajusta o que faltou.
lines: Vou ler duas vezes um resumo curto da reunião do shopping. Ouça e reconstrua a ata em voz alta.
Read twice: 'We decided the facade work starts Monday. Paulo is the owner, due date next Friday. We parked the parking-lot lighting for the next meeting.'
Agora reconstrua usando 'to take minutes', 'owner' e 'due date'.
Compare com o original e diga o que faltou.
Read a second short summary and have him reconstruct it again.

practiceBank.title: Metade da pauta em cada mão
practiceBank.how: Cada lado tem metade dos 'agenda items'. O aluno pergunta para montar a 'agenda' completa da quinzenal e depois a lê em voz alta na ordem. Professor só fornece itens quando perguntado corretamente.
lines: Você tem metade dos agenda items, eu tenho a outra. Pergunte para montar a pauta completa.
Wait for him to ask correctly: 'What's the next agenda item?' before you give one.
Provide only when asked: 'Item three is the elevator inspection.'
Once complete, have him read the full agenda aloud in order.
Ask: 'Is anything missing from the agenda for today?'

practiceBank.title: Diga a frase de controle de reunião
practiceBank.how: Professor cria situações ('a reunião está atrasada', 'esse tema é para depois') e o aluno responde com a expressão-alvo ('let's keep us to time', 'let's park that'). Ritmo rápido, sem tradução.
lines: Situação: a reunião está atrasada. Resposta-alvo: 'Let's keep us to time.'
Situação: alguém traz um tema fora da pauta. Resposta-alvo: 'Let's park that for the parking lot.'
Situação: você precisa registrar a decisão. Resposta-alvo: 'I'll take the minutes.'
Situação: hora de dar tarefas. Resposta-alvo: 'Let's assign the action items.'
Ritmo rápido, sem tradução. Dispare as quatro de novo fora de ordem.

practiceBank.title: Você é quem conduz
practiceBank.how: Aluno na 'hot seat' como chair da reunião; professor lança curveballs (alguém fala fora da pauta, outro pede prazo). Aluno gerencia tudo falando, usando 'recap email', 'to assign', 'to keep us to time'.
lines: Você é o chair da quinzenal. Abra e conduza — eu lanço curveballs.
Curveball: 'Sorry to jump in, but what about the roof leak?' — você usa 'parking lot'.
Curveball: 'I need two more weeks on my action item.' — você renegocia.
Curveball: 'We're running over time.' — você responde com 'let's keep us to time'.
Close with: 'I'll send a recap email and assign the action items.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: O recap email falado
practiceBank.how: O aluno 'dita' em voz alta o 'recap email' de uma reunião sobre o shopping: o que foi decidido, quem é 'owner', qual o 'due date'. Professor checa se cada action item tem dono e prazo.
lines: Dite o recap email em voz alta. Start with: 'Hi team, here's a quick recap of today's meeting on the mall project.'
State each decision made about the shopping center.
For each action item, name the owner and the due date.
Vou checar: cada action item tem dono e prazo?
End with: 'Please confirm by end of day. Thanks!'

practiceBank.title: Quem é o owner?
practiceBank.how: Professor dispara decisões soltas e o aluno responde quem é 'owner' e o 'due date', depois inverte e pergunta de volta. Mantém o foco em 'action item' e 'by end of day' em ritmo ágil.
lines: Quem é o owner? 'We decided to fix the parking lot lighting — who's the owner and the due date?'
'The facade inspection — who owns it and when is it due?'
'The recap email to the client — owner and due date?'
'The elevator delay report — by end of day, who?'
Agora inverta: você pergunta de volta e eu respondo o owner e a due date.
Mantenha o ritmo ágil em 'action item' e 'by end of day'.

practiceBank.title: Reunião descarrilando
practiceBank.how: Cenário: a quinzenal virou discussão técnica fora da pauta. O aluno precisa, falando, retomar o controle com 'parking lot' e fechar com action items. Professor encena o participante prolixo.
lines: Cenário: a quinzenal virou discussão técnica sobre concreto, fora da pauta. Retome o controle falando.
Eu sou o participante prolixo: 'And the concrete mix, you know, last project we...'
Você corta com: 'Let me park that. Let's keep us to time.'
Bring it back: 'Back to our agenda for today.'
Close with action items, each with an owner and a due date.
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: Fechar a pauta em 5 minutos
practiceBank.how: Com cronômetro, o aluno deve fechar uma agenda de 3 itens em 5 minutos, atribuindo owners e due dates antes do tempo acabar. Professor é o cliente que enrola; o aluno usa 'to keep us to time'.
lines: Cronômetro de 5 minutos. Feche uma agenda de 3 itens, atribuindo owners e due dates.
Eu sou o cliente que enrola: 'Hold on, tell me more about that one.'
Você usa 'to keep us to time' para avançar.
Por item: state the decision, name the owner, set the due date.
Beat the clock: 'Let's wrap up — three action items, all assigned.'
(Corrija só no final.)

practiceBank.title: 60s de abertura de reunião
practiceBank.how: O aluno grava a abertura de uma reunião quinzenal do shopping em 60s, apresentando a 'agenda' e o objetivo. Reouve e o professor marca clareza de pauta e uso de 'agenda item'.
lines: Grave 60s abrindo a quinzenal do shopping. Start with: 'Good morning, welcome to our biweekly meeting.'
Present the agenda for today and state the objective of the meeting.
Name at least two agenda items out loud.
Reouça a gravação comigo.
Eu marco clareza da pauta e o uso de 'agenda item'.

practiceBank.title: Levanta os itens e reporta
practiceBank.how: O aluno 'entrevista' o professor (que faz vários membros da equipe) para coletar tópicos da próxima reunião, depois reporta de volta organizando-os em 'agenda items'. Pratica perguntar e sintetizar falando.
lines: Você me entrevista para coletar tópicos da próxima reunião. Eu faço vários membros da equipe.
Persona 1: 'I want to discuss the delivery delays.' — você anota como agenda item.
Persona 2: 'We need to talk about the client's budget cut.'
Persona 3: 'The safety audit results should be on there.'
Now report back: organize everything into agenda items, in order, out loud.

leadIn: Who usually sets the agenda for your meetings with the American client?
Do you take the minutes yourself, or does someone else?
What's one action item you assigned this week, and to which owner?
When a meeting runs long, how do you keep everyone to time?
After a meeting on the mall project, do you send a recap email?

pill.tip: Sem ênfase, 'for' reduz a 'fer' (schwa), não 'fôr'. 'For the team' soa como 'fer-dâ-tim'.
pill.sample: This is for the team and for the client.

lessons.title: Holidays & traditions (Thanksgiving, July 4th)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa com naturalidade sobre feriados e tradições americanas — como Thanksgiving e o Quatro de Julho — criando conexão genuína com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
In 18- to 24-month projects, the relationship with the American client runs largely on light conversations. Knowing how to talk about holidays like Thanksgiving (Dia de Acao de Gracas) and the Fourth of July (Quatro de Julho) opens human doors that no technical report can. These are dates when families gather (se reunem) and show gratitude (gratidao).

These holidays have simple symbols that are easy to comment on: the turkey (peru) at Thanksgiving, the fireworks (fogos de artificio) and cookouts (churrascos ao ar livre) on the Fourth of July. Many Americans use the long weekend (feriado prolongado) for a road trip (viagem de carro) or to recharge (recarregar as energias) with family.

For the Racional executive, mentioning these topics at the start of a call or dinner creates connection. Asking "Did you host Thanksgiving this year?" shows genuine interest and cultural care. That's exactly what sets apart purely functional communication from a relationship of trust with North American key accounts.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora leves: "How was your Thanksgiving?", "Did you do anything for the Fourth of July?" e "It's a long weekend, time to recharge."

O tom aqui é leve e amigável, não técnico.
lessons.situation: Antes de começar uma call, você quer criar conexão. O cliente acabou de voltar de um feriado americano e você puxa uma conversa leve.
lessons.context: Holidays are a great way to connect. On Thanksgiving, families gather and share gratitude. They eat turkey and enjoy a long weekend. The next day, they eat the leftovers. On the Fourth of July, people watch fireworks. Many have a cookout in the yard. Some take a road trip to visit family. It is a good time to recharge. So before a call, I like to ask: "How was your holiday?" A small question builds a real connection.

vocab.example: Thanksgiving is in November.
The Fourth of July is a big holiday.
Families gather for dinner.
They share gratitude at the table.
We eat turkey on Thanksgiving.
We watch fireworks at night.
They have a cookout in the yard.
It is a long weekend this week.
Did you host the dinner?
We eat the leftovers the next day.
They take a road trip to the coast.
I use the weekend to recharge.
There is a parade in the town.

practiceBank.title: Small talk pós-feriado
practiceBank.how: Professor é o cliente americano que acabou de voltar do Thanksgiving. O aluno puxa conversa leve perguntando como foi, usando 'to gather', 'leftovers', 'a long weekend'. Foco em soar natural e criar conexão antes da call do shopping.

Ask: 'How was your Thanksgiving? Did you get to gather with family?'
Eu respondo: 'It was great, the whole family came over.' — você reage com 'leftovers' e 'a long weekend'.

practiceBank.title: Conte um feriado brasileiro em troca
practiceBank.how: Depois de ouvir sobre o feriado do cliente, o aluno conta um feriado seu (Natal, Carnaval) usando estruturas equivalentes ('to gather', 'to host', 'to recharge'). Professor reage e compara com Thanksgiving.

Start with: 'In Brazil, we have something similar. At Christmas, we gather...'
Use 'to host' and 'to recharge' naturally.
Eu reajo e comparo com Thanksgiving: 'Oh, just like our turkey dinner!'
Respond to my comparison and keep the chat flowing.

practiceBank.title: Bingo de tradições
practiceBank.how: Professor encarna várias pessoas; o aluno circula com perguntas tipo 'Did you host a cookout?', 'Did you watch the fireworks?' para preencher um cartão. Usa o vocab de feriados em perguntas reais. Professor varia respostas.

practiceBank.title: Conecte feriado e palavra
practiceBank.how: Professor diz uma cena ('churrasco no quintal', 'sobras na geladeira') e o aluno responde com o termo certo ('a cookout', 'leftovers'). Rápido, sem tradução; professor só dá a deixa visual/verbal.
lines: Cena: churrasco no quintal. Resposta-alvo: 'a cookout'.
Cena: sobras na geladeira depois do jantar. Resposta-alvo: 'leftovers'.
Cena: fogos no céu no Quatro de Julho. Resposta-alvo: 'fireworks'.
Cena: a família toda se reunindo. Resposta-alvo: 'to gather'.
Rápido, sem tradução. Repita fora de ordem.

practiceBank.title: Descreva a cena do 4 de Julho
practiceBank.how: Professor mostra/descreve uma imagem do Fourth of July (parade, fireworks, cookout). O aluno descreve a cena em voz alta usando 'fireworks', 'a parade', 'a cookout'. Professor pede detalhes sensoriais.

Agora você pergunta de volta e eu respondo. Mantenha o tom leve.

practiceBank.title: Thanksgiving x feriado brasileiro
practiceBank.how: O aluno compara, falando, Thanksgiving com um feriado brasileiro de reunião familiar, dando opinião sobre semelhanças ('we also gather', 'we also have leftovers'). Professor adiciona nuances culturais para o aluno reagir.

Reouça comigo.

lessons.title: First meeting & introductions
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz a abertura de uma primeira reunião em inglês simples — se apresenta, apresenta a Racional e os participantes — com um cliente norte-americano novo.
lessons.overview:
The first meeting with a new client sets the tone for the entire project. For Racional, which competes for contracts with clients like Microsoft and Amazon, a strong opening is half the battle. It all starts when you introduce yourself (se apresenta) and say the classic phrase: It's a pleasure to meet you (e um prazer conhece-lo), especially when the meeting is in person (presencial).

In an opening, you present your background (historico/experiencia), explain that you are on the board (na diretoria), and kick things off (da inicio) with the agenda for today (pauta de hoje). It's the moment to set expectations (alinhar expectativas) and introduce your counterpart (contraparte) - the equivalent person on the other side.

The American client values a warm but objective opening: a warm welcome (boas-vindas calorosas), followed by clarity about what will be covered. When you say "I look forward to working with you" and hand it over (passa a palavra) to a colleague, you project the strategic posture expected of a Racional Board executive. That's how you build trust from the very first minute.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "It's a pleasure to meet you.", "Let me kick things off with the agenda." e "I look forward to working with you."

Pratique-as como blocos prontos para a primeira reunião.
lessons.situation: Você lidera a primeira reunião com um cliente americano novo. Precisa se apresentar, apresentar a Racional e a equipe, e dar início à pauta.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone. It's a pleasure to meet you in person. Let me introduce myself. I am on the board of Racional. Racional is a Brazilian builder with more than fifty years. Let me kick things off with the agenda for today. First, I will give a short background. Then we set expectations together. This is my counterpart, Ana. She runs our project team. A warm welcome to all of you. I look forward to working with you. Now I hand it over to Ana.

lessons.title: Conference calls & virtual meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você participa e conduz conference calls em inglês simples — administrando áudio, turnos de fala e problemas técnicos — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
A large share of Racional's monthly and biweekly meetings with U.S. clients happens over virtual calls. Knowing how to navigate a conference call in English is now a basic governance skill. The terms start with the audio: being on mute (mudo), to unmute (desmutar), and to share your screen (compartilhar a tela) to show a schedule or a floor plan.

Calls have their own problems. Sometimes people talk over each other (falam ao mesmo tempo), the connection breaks up (fica falhando), there is lag (atraso de audio), or someone drops off the call (cai da chamada). Leading well means inviting people to go ahead (prosseguir) and chime in (dar uma contribuicao), and using the chat (o chat) when needed.

For the Racional executive, controlling the dynamics of a call projects leadership even from a distance. Starting with a round of intros (rodada de apresentacoes), managing the turns, and wrapping up the call (encerrar a chamada) with a recap before we close (resumo antes de fechar) keeps the meeting productive and conveys the organization that American key accounts expect.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "You're on mute.", "Can you share your screen?" e "Let's do a quick recap before we close."

São frases curtas que você usa em quase toda call.
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma conference call com o cliente americano. Precisa administrar o áudio, organizar os turnos de fala e encerrar com um resumo.
lessons.context: Let's start with a round of intros. Can everyone hear me? You're on mute, please unmute. Can you share your screen? We see your schedule now. Sorry, the line breaks up a little. There is some lag today. Please go ahead and finish your point. Does anyone want to chime in? You can also use the chat. One person dropped off the call. Let's wait one minute. Now let's do a quick recap before we close.

lessons.title: Brainstorming & ideation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma sessão de brainstorming em inglês simples — convida ideias, constrói sobre o que os outros dizem e organiza as opções — com a equipe do cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
In complex Racional projects - a hyperscale data center or a hospital with tight deadlines - many solutions come out of brainstorming sessions with the client. Leading that conversation in English calls for its own vocabulary. It starts with inviting ideas: to put options on the table (colocar opcoes na mesa) and to throw out an idea (lancar uma ideia), without fear of being wrong.

The secret of brainstorming is building together. You encourage the team to bounce ideas around (trocar ideias livremente), to expand on an idea (desenvolver uma ideia), and to defer judgment (adiar o julgamento) - remembering that there are no bad ideas (nao ha ideias ruins) at this point. A good idea can spark (faisca/inspirar) an even better one.

After generating many options, it's time to focus: to narrow down (reduzir) to a shortlist (lista curta), prioritize (priorizar), and flesh out (detalhar) the best ones. For the Racional executive, knowing how to open, lead, and converge on (convergir para) a decision projects collaborative leadership - exactly what creates value and trust with the American client's team.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "Let's put some options on the table.", "There are no bad ideas here." e "Let's narrow down to a shortlist."

Pratique abrir o brainstorming e depois fechar com foco.
lessons.situation: Você conduz uma sessão de brainstorming com a equipe do cliente americano para resolver um desafio do projeto. Precisa convidar ideias e organizar as melhores.
lessons.context: Let's put some options on the table. Please throw out any idea. There are no bad ideas here. Let's defer judgment for now. One idea can spark another idea. Feel free to expand on what your colleague said. Let's bounce ideas around. Now let's narrow down the list. We pick a shortlist of three. Then we prioritize and flesh out the best one. Good. We converge on a clear next step.

vocab.en: to put options on the table

Can you expand on that idea?
Let's bounce ideas around.
Let's defer judgment for now.

lessons.title: Status updates (weekly / monthly)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em inglês simples, um status update semanal ou mensal a um cliente americano — reportando progresso, riscos e próximos passos com clareza.
lessons.overview:
The status update (atualizacao de status) is the most frequently repeated meeting in a Racional project. On a hyperscale data center for a client like Microsoft, the cycle lasts 18 to 24 months, and almost every week or every month someone from the board needs to tell the client where the project stands. It's not a long conversation: it's a short, factual report on what moved forward, what is concerning, and what comes next.

The American client values directness. That's why the headline first (comecar pela conclusao) technique works so well: you open with a verdict sentence, like "We are on track", and only then go into the details. Next, you show the progress to date (progresso ate aqui) and use to flag (sinalizar) to point out any risk early, before it becomes a bigger problem.

For an Executive Board member, this ritual is also an exercise in trust. Calmly reporting a long-lead item (item de prazo longo) that may slip (atrasar), already with a mitigation plan (plano de mitigacao), shows control. That's how Racional sustains the long-term relationship with its North American key accounts on offices, hospitals, shopping centers, and data centers.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora para usar na prática: "Let me start with the headline" para abrir, "Since our last update, we completed..." para reportar o avanço, e "I want to flag one risk" para sinalizar uma atenção.

A ordem é sempre a mesma: veredito primeiro, progresso depois, risco com plano e próximos passos. Frases curtas, tom calmo.
lessons.situation: Na reunião mensal de um data center, o cliente americano pede o status do projeto. Você abre com o headline e percorre progresso, risco e próximos passos.
lessons.context: Let me start with the headline: we are on track for next month. Since our last update, we finished the foundation. We are a little ahead of schedule on the structure. I want to flag one risk early. A long-lead item could slip by two weeks. But we have a mitigation plan. I will send a short recap today, and I will keep you posted.

lessons.title: Hosting clients in Brazil
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você recebe e acompanha, em inglês simples, um cliente americano em visita ao Brasil — do aeroporto ao jantar — como um anfitrião caloroso.
lessons.overview:
This is a lesson about relationship (relacionamento), not grammar. When an American client travels to Brazil to visit a Racional project, the hours outside the meeting room matter as much as the meeting itself. Being a good host (anfitriao) in English is what turns a supplier into a partner for many years.

In an 18- to 24-month project, the client will come to Brazil more than once. Hosting well means taking care of simple things: picking the person up at the airport (to pick someone up), showing them the city (to show someone around), and keeping the first day light because of jet lag (cansaco da viagem). Small questions like "How was the flight?" show genuine care.

Brazilian hospitality is already your edge. The invitation to a steakhouse (churrascaria), always with a no pressure (sem pressao) for someone who is tired, closes the day with warmth. For an Executive Board member at Racional, knowing how to say all of this in English is what creates the long-term bond with North American key accounts.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora calorosas: "Welcome to São Paulo! How was the flight?", "Let me show you around" e "Is there anything you'd like to try?".

O tom é leve e pessoal. Frases curtas, sempre com a opção de descanso para quem chega com jet lag.

lessons.context: Welcome to São Paulo! How was the flight? You must be tired, so we kept today light. The driver is outside, and your hotel is twenty minutes away. Tonight, if you are up for it, I would love to take you to a great Brazilian steakhouse. But no pressure. We can keep it easy if you want to rest.

lessons.title: War rooms & crisis meetings
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz, em inglês simples, uma war room ou reunião de crise com um cliente americano — mantendo o foco, definindo o caminho e os responsáveis.
lessons.overview:
A war room is the meeting that brings the right people together when something goes wrong on a project. On a Racional project — a hospital, a shopping center, or a data center — an equipment delay or a supplier problem can bring the work to a halt. The war room exists to contain the impact quickly, calmly, and with method.

The American client expects firmness and clarity at this moment. The phrase here's what we know opens the meeting with the facts. Then the group looks for the root cause, sets an action owner for each task, and agrees on the path forward. There is no hunting for someone to blame: the focus is the solution.

For a member of the Executive Board, leading a crisis meeting means showing presence under pressure. Knowing how to keep a cool head, to take ownership, and to set a checkpoint for the next day is what conveys confidence to the client and protects the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora para a crise: "Let's stay focused" para abrir, "Here's what we know" para os fatos e "Here is the path forward" para a solução.

O tom é calmo e firme. Cada ação tem um dono e uma data; a reunião termina com um próximo checkpoint.
lessons.situation: Um item crítico atrasou no data center e a entrega está em risco. Você abre uma war room com o cliente americano para conter o impacto e definir o caminho.
lessons.context: Let's stay focused. Here is what we know. One key item is late, and this puts the deadline at risk. We are looking at the root cause now. For each action, we will name an owner today. Here is the path forward. I will take ownership of the supplier call. Let's keep a cool head and meet again tomorrow for a checkpoint.

We need a short crisis meeting.

Let's find the root cause first.

We will escalate if needed.
Let's keep a cool head.

I will take ownership of this.
Let's set a checkpoint tomorrow.

lessons.title: Steering committees
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reporta, em inglês simples, a um steering committee com cliente americano — usando green, amber e red e pedindo as decisões que precisa.
lessons.overview:
The steering committee is the highest-level meeting of a project. It is where the client's and Racional's sponsors look at the overall health of the work and make the big decisions. On a data center or a shopping center, this is where changes to scope, schedule, and budget are approved — not the day-to-day details.

The committee speaks the language of the traffic light: green, amber, and red to show the project health. You report at a high level, without going into technical detail, and you say clearly where you need a decision: we need a decision on.

For a member of Racional's Executive Board, the steering committee is the stage for governance. Knowing how to seek approval, how to present a recommendation, and how to record everything in a decision log is what keeps the project under control and the North American client's trust steady over the 18 to 24 months.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora de governança: "Overall, the project is green" para a saúde, "We need a decision on..." para o pedido e "My recommendation is..." para conduzir.

O tom é alto nível: poucos números, decisões claras e tudo registrado no decision log.
lessons.situation: No steering committee mensal do shopping center, você reporta a saúde do projeto e pede uma decisão sobre uma mudança de escopo.
lessons.context: Good morning. I will report at a high level. Overall, the project is green. One area is amber: a long-lead item. We need a decision on a change in scope today. My recommendation is to approve it now. This keeps us on time. I will add the decision to the log. The technical detail is out of scope for today.

vocab.example: The steering committee meets today.
This is a governance meeting.
The client sponsor is here.
Let me show the project health.
The project is green this month.

vocab.en: to report at a high level
vocab.example: I will report at a high level.
We need a decision on the budget.
Can we approve this today?
There is a small change in scope.
We escalate this to the committee.
My recommendation is to wait.
We seek approval for the change.
I will add it to the decision log.
That is out of scope for today.

lessons.title: Negotiation fundamentals (BATNA, ZOPA)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você entende e usa, em inglês simples, as bases da negociação — BATNA, ZOPA, leverage e common ground — com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Every contract negotiation at Racional rests on a few fundamentals worth knowing in English. Your BATNA is your best option if the deal falls through — your plan B. The ZOPA is the range where both sides can close, between the client's limit and yours. And the walk-away point is the price below which it is not worth going forward.

Before negotiating schedule, scope, and price for a data center or a shopping center, you need to come prepared. Whoever knows their leverage and their negotiating position looks for common ground and negotiates with the game of give and take, without conceding too much.

The American client tends to negotiate in a direct and well-prepared way. For a member of Racional's Executive Board, understanding the bottom line and the right concession avoids to leave money on the table and protects the project's margin without breaking the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora de negociação: "Let's find common ground", "This is our bottom line" e "I came prepared".

O tom é firme e respeitoso. Você conhece seu plano B (BATNA) e a faixa de acordo (ZOPA) antes de sentar à mesa.
lessons.situation: Antes de negociar o preço de um contrato com um cliente americano, você revisa sua BATNA, sua ZOPA e o seu walk-away point com a equipe.
lessons.context: Let's get ready for the talk. We need to know our BATNA, our best other option. We also need our walk-away point. The ZOPA is the range where both sides can agree. Our leverage is good this time. Let's find common ground and use give and take. This is our bottom line, and I came prepared.

vocab.example: Our BATNA is strong this time.
The ZOPA is small here.
We have a clear walk-away point.
Let's anchor with a fair price.
Our leverage is good now.
Let's find common ground.
A deal needs give and take.
We can offer one concession.
This is our bottom line.
We are better off with plan B.
Our negotiating position is clear.
Let's try to settle today.

vocab.en: to leave money on the table
vocab.example: We don't want to leave money on the table.
Always come prepared.

exercises.explanation: Plano B, faixa e limite. É o preparo que evita deixar dinheiro na mesa.

lessons.title: Negotiation tactics & language
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa, em inglês simples, táticas e frases de negociação — trocas condicionais, segurar o preço e o trial close — com um cliente americano.
lessons.overview:
Knowing the fundamentals is not enough: at the table, you need the right phrases ready on the tip of your tongue. The most useful tactic is the conditional concession: never give something away for free, always trade. The structure if... then... is the heart of it — "If you move the date, then we hold the price."

In a schedule or price negotiation on a Racional project, you will to push back respectfully, show that you listened with I hear you, and measure the space that remains with wiggle room. Sometimes the way out is to split the difference; other times it is to hold the price and to stay firm.

Near the end, the trial close tests the agreement without pressure: are we good to move ahead? For a member of the Executive Board, knowing how to trade, how to lock in the deal, and how to judge when to give ground is what closes good contracts with American clients without wearing down the long-term relationship.
lessons.intro:
Vamos firmar três frases-âncora de tática: "If you do X, then we can do Y" para trocar, "I hear you, but we need to hold the price" para rebater e "Are we good to move ahead?" para testar o fechamento.

O tom é colaborativo e firme. Toda concessão vem com uma troca; nada é dado de graça.
lessons.situation: Na reta final da negociação do contrato, o cliente americano pede um desconto. Você usa trocas condicionais e um trial close para fechar.
lessons.context: I hear you on the price. But we need to hold the price here. Let's trade instead. If you move the date by two weeks, then we can add the extra work. We have little wiggle room left. Maybe we can split the difference. So, are we good to move ahead and lock in the deal?

lessons.title: American cities & business hubs
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conversa, em inglês simples, sobre cidades e polos de negócio dos Estados Unidos — conectando-se ao cliente a partir de onde ele vive e trabalha.
lessons.overview:
This lesson is about connection, not grammar. The North American client speaks naturally about the city where they live and about the country's major business hubs. When you comment on their city with interest — "Austin? I hear it is a great tech hub" — you show genuine attention and build rapport before the meeting even begins.

A quick and useful map for Racional: New York and the East Coast concentrate finance; Silicon Valley and Seattle, on the West Coast, bring together the big technology companies — Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, clients in the hyperscale data center segment; Texas, with Austin and Dallas, is growing fast and attracting many new projects. Knowing this terrain helps you understand where the client is coming from and why they think the way they do.

The rule is simple: connect the client's city to their work and ask a short, curious question. Use anchor phrases like "Where are you based?", "I've heard great things about it", and "What's it like there?" In a few seconds, geography turns into conversation, and conversation turns into a long-term relationship with the key account.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três frases-âncora: "Where are you based?" (onde você mora?), "I've heard great things about it." (ouvi falar muito bem de lá) e "What's it like there?" (como é por lá?).

Use o vocabulário do tema — tech hub, booming, cost of living — para comentar a cidade e devolver com uma pergunta curiosa.
lessons.situation: Num café antes da reunião, o cliente americano diz que mora em Austin. Você puxa uma conversa leve sobre a cidade e os polos de tecnologia dos EUA.
lessons.context: Oh, you are based in Austin? Nice! I hear it is a great tech hub now. The tech market there is booming. Many companies move to Texas because the cost of living is good. I was only on the East Coast, in New York. What is Austin like? I want to visit one day.

lessons.title: Hard bargaining vs. principled negotiation
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você diferencia, em inglês simples, a barganha dura da negociação por princípios — falando de interesses, critérios e ganho mútuo com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
As a Board executive, you do not negotiate to win a fight: you negotiate to build a relationship of 18 to 24 months. This lesson separates two styles. Hard bargaining treats the other side as an opponent and only disputes who gives in first. Principled negotiation attacks the problem, not the person, and seeks an agreement that is fair for both sides.

The secret is to separate the position (what each side asks for) from the interest (the real reason behind the request) and to lean on objective criteria (market price, schedules, benchmarks). When the client asks for a hard number, you ask why, look for common ground, and aim for the win-win. On a project with 620+ deliverables like Racional's, scope and risk are discussed with data, not with pressure.

The golden rule: be firm on the problem and gentle with the person. With the American client, who values directness, firmness combined with respect builds credibility. Simple anchor phrases — "What is the interest behind that?" and "Let's find common ground" — keep the conversation professional and protect the long-term partnership.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe três âncoras: "What is the interest behind that?" (qual é o interesse por trás disso?), "Let's find common ground." (vamos achar um terreno comum) e "We want a win-win." (queremos um ganha-ganha).

Foque no interest por trás do número, use objective criteria e mantenha o tom firme, mas respeitoso.
lessons.situation: Numa negociação de contrato, o cliente americano abre com uma postura dura sobre preço. Você leva a conversa para os interesses reais e para critérios objetivos.
lessons.context: I hear your number. But let's talk about the interest behind it, not only the price. I don't want this to be a fight. If we look at objective criteria, like market prices and scope, we can find common ground. We want a win-win, because this is a long partnership.

lessons.title: Pricing negotiations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você negocia preço em inglês simples — justificando valor, falando de margem e concessões — com um cliente norte-americano.
lessons.overview:
Every construction negotiation eventually reaches price. As a Racional executive, you do not compete on number alone: you defend value. The central idea of this lesson is value-based pricing: showing the client what they receive — on-time delivery, safety, technical quality — and not just cutting cost. When you talk about price with confidence, the client understands why Racional charges what it charges.

You will learn how to justify the price and how to talk about margin and bottom line. You will learn the game of concessions: every time you give something, you ask for something in return — that is the trade-off. You will also see everyday executive terms such as ballpark figure, payment terms, and to lock in a price, along with the risk of a cost overrun on an 18-to-24-month project.

The golden rule with the American client: add value, not cut cost. Directness does not mean automatic discount. If the number has to come down, trade it for scope, schedule, or terms — never give a discount for free. And know when to walk away to protect the company's margin and credibility.
lessons.intro:
Antes da prática, fixe duas âncoras: "Let me justify the price." (deixe-me justificar o preço) e "We add value, we don't just cut cost." (nós agregamos valor, não só cortamos custo).

Lembre o jogo das concessões: cada vez que você cede, peça algo em troca (trade-off).
lessons.situation: O cliente americano pede um desconto grande. Você justifica o preço pelo valor e propõe uma troca em vez de simplesmente baixar o número.
lessons.context: I understand you want a lower number. But let me justify the price first. We don't just cut cost. We add value: we deliver on time and with high quality. If you need a lower price, let's make a trade-off. We can change the scope or the payment terms. That way, we both win.

vocab.example: Let me justify the price.
We use value-based pricing.
